definition_zh: 使恶化；加重；激怒；使恼火
definition_en: to make a problem, illness, or situation worse, or to annoy someone
core_image: 往已经沉重的担子上再压一块石头
scene: 病人的伤口还没愈合，他又执意下地干活。 Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 aggravate 是「使恶化」（第 1 个义项：使问题或病情变得更严重）；句意为缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。图中可辨识物件：绷带、拐杖、病床。

pos.zh: 动词：使恶化；加重；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由 aggravate 加 -ion 构成，义为「加重；恶化；激怒」
由 aggravate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的；使恶化的」
由 aggravate 加 -ed 构成，义为「加重的；被激怒的」

senses.title: To make a condition worse
senses.definition: to make an illness, injury, or bad situation more serious
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤势或糟糕的局面变得更加严重
senses.example: Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。
senses.why: Latin gravis meant heavy; adding ad- 'toward' made aggravare 'to add weight', so the word pictures a load made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gravis 意为「沉重」；加上 ad-「朝向」构成 aggravare「加重」，词的画面就是一担更沉的负荷。

senses.title: To add to a burden
senses.definition: to increase the weight of a burden, cost, or difficulty that already exists
senses.definitionCN: 增加原有负担、成本或困难的分量
senses.example: The new tax aggravated the burden on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新税加重了小店铺的负担。
senses.why: The same image works for money and work: whatever is already heavy can be made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 同样的画面也适用于金钱与工作：本来沉重的东西还能再被压重。

senses.title: To provoke or annoy
senses.definition: to make someone angry or irritated, especially by repeated behavior
senses.definitionCN: 使人生气或烦躁，尤因反复出现的行为
senses.example: His endless questions aggravated the tired teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了的问题让疲惫的老师很恼火。
senses.why: An added weight is also felt on the nerves; the word shifted from burdens on the body to burdens on the temper.
senses.whyCN: 加在身上的重量也会压在神经上；词义于是从身体的负担转到脾气的负担。

senses.title: To make a legal offence graver
senses.definition: to make an offence more serious in law, usually by an added circumstance such as a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上使罪行更严重，通常因使用武器等附加情节
senses.example: The theft was aggravated by the use of a weapon.
senses.exampleCN: 由于使用了武器，这起盗窃案被认定为加重情节。
senses.why: Law keeps the literal sense: one fact adds weight to another, and the scale of guilt goes up.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了字面义：一个事实给另一个事实增加重量，罪责的天平随之上升。

senses.title: To intensify a conflict
senses.definition: to make hostility or tension between people or groups stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使人与人、群体与群体之间的敌意或紧张变得更强
senses.example: The speech aggravated the tension between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲加剧了两个群体之间的紧张关系。
senses.why: Tension is another kind of load; words can add to it just as weight adds to a cart.
senses.whyCN: 紧张也是一种负荷；言语能像重量压在车上那样，给它再加一层。

senses.title: To make pain sharper
senses.definition: to increase physical pain, especially by movement or pressure on a hurt part
senses.definitionCN: 使身体的疼痛更强，尤因活动或压迫受伤部位
senses.example: Walking up the stairs aggravated the pain in her back.
senses.exampleCN: 上楼梯使她背部的疼痛加剧了。
senses.why: Pain is the most bodily of burdens; anything that presses on it literally adds weight.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛是最身体化的负担；任何压上去的动作都在字面上增加重量。

intro.en: Aggravate is literally 'to add weight', built in Latin from ad- and gravis.
intro.cn: aggravate 字面就是「增加重量」，由拉丁语的 ad- 与 gravis 构成。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy, weighty, or serious, and it also gave English grave, gravity and grief.
items.cn: gravis 意为「沉重的、有分量的、严重的」，也生出英语的 grave、gravity 与 grief。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus gravare 'to weigh down' produced aggravare, to add weight or make heavier.
items.cn: ad-「向」加上 gravare「压重」构成 aggravare，意为「加重、使更沉」。

items.en: The past participle aggravated described something made heavier or more serious.
items.cn: 过去分词 aggravatus 描述被加重、变得更严重的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the word for making a disease or burden worse, the sense that still dominates.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用来指使疾病或负担加重，这一含义至今占主导。

items.en: A colloquial sense 'to annoy' appeared later and is often criticised, though it is now widespread.
items.cn: 「使恼火」这一口语义出现较晚，常被批评，但如今已广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making things worse.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示「使变糟」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something worse, or a source of annoyance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加重；恶化」，也指令人恼火的事。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning making a situation worse or making someone annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「使恶化的；令人恼火的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing something made worse, or a person who is annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加重的；被激怒的」。

entries.definition: To become or make something worse in quality or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「恶化；使更糟」，指质量或状况变差。

entries.definition: To make something stronger or more extreme in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加强；加剧」，指程度变得更强或更极端。

entries.definition: To make a bad situation or feeling even worse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恶化；使加剧」，多用于糟糕的局面或情绪。

normalIntro.en: These hooks turn the word into a picture of added weight and rising irritation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把词义化成「加重」与「火气上升」的画面。

normal.en: AGGRAVATE hides grave: a grave situation gets heavier.
normal.cn: aggravate 里藏着 grave：严重的局面会变得更沉重。

normal.en: Picture a porter adding one more stone to an already heavy sack.
normal.cn: 想象搬运工往已经很重的袋子里再塞一块石头。

normal.en: A bad knee plus a long walk equals aggravation.
normal.cn: 一只坏膝盖加上一段长路，就是「加重」。

normal.en: When words add weight to a quarrel, they aggravate it.
normal.cn: 当言语给争吵增加重量时，就是把矛盾加剧。

normal.en: Annoyance is weight on the nerves, so the same word serves both senses.
normal.cn: 恼火是压神经上的重量，所以同一个词能兼指两义。

abstract.en: To aggravate is to make the load heavier without adding anything useful.
abstract.cn: 加剧就是在没有增添任何有益之物的情况下，把负荷压得更重。

abstract.en: The word keeps the body's scales even when it speaks of feelings.
abstract.cn: 即便说的是情绪，这个词仍带着身体的天平。

abstract.en: Many problems grow worse because someone keeps pressing on them.
abstract.cn: 许多问题之所以恶化，是因为总有人在上面继续施压。

examples.en: Scratching the rash will only aggravate it.
examples.cn: 抓挠皮疹只会使它更严重。

examples.en: The delay aggravated the anger of the waiting crowd.
examples.cn: 延误使等候人群的怒气更盛。

examples.en: His loud jokes began to aggravate the tired nurses.
examples.cn: 他响亮的笑话开始让疲惫的护士们恼火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挨个累」：一件件事挨个累加上去，情况就越来越糟。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ gravis（沉重的、严重的）构成 aggravare（加重），再经过去分词 aggravatus 进入英语，核心意象是「往已有的负担上再加重量」。

sensesIntro.en: The single image of added weight spreads over illness, burdens, temper, law, conflict and physical pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 「增加重量」这一个意象，扩展到病情、负担、脾气、法律、冲突与身体的疼痛。

core.en: ADD WEIGHT TO WHAT IS ALREADY HEAVY
core.cn: 给已经沉重的再加重量

branches.en: a disease or injury made worse
branches.cn: 病情或伤势被恶化

branches.en: tension between people made stronger
branches.cn: 人与人之间的紧张被加剧

branches.en: physical pain made sharper
branches.cn: 身体的疼痛被加强

branches.en: a burden made heavier
branches.cn: 负担被压得更重

branches.en: temper irritated or guilt weighed up by law
branches.cn: 脾气被激怒，或罪责在法律上被加重

intro.en: Aggravate sits on the Latin root gravis 'heavy', which also underlies several English words about weight and seriousness.
intro.cn: aggravate 立在拉丁词根 gravis「沉重」上，英语中若干表示重量与严重的词也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: From gravis Latin built gravare and gravitas, and English later added its own suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语由 gravis 造出 gravare 与 gravitas，英语后来又加上自己的后缀。

items.meaning: the act of making worse, or something that annoys
items.meaningCN: 加重；恶化；令人恼火的事
items.example: The extra paperwork was pure aggravation.
items.exampleCN: 额外的文书工作纯粹令人恼火。

items.meaning: making a situation worse or making someone angry
items.example: The aggravating noise continued all night.
items.exampleCN: 那恼人的噪音持续了一整夜。

items.example: The aggravated injury kept him home.
items.exampleCN: 加重的伤势使他只能待在家里。

items.meaning: in a way that annoys or worsens
items.example: He smiled aggravatingly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 他恼人地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: The doctor spoke of a grave risk.
items.exampleCN: 医生谈到了一种严重的风险。

items.meaning: the force that pulls things down, or serious importance
items.example: Gravity pulled the ball back to earth.

items.meaning: to move toward something as if pulled
items.example: Young readers gravitate toward that series.
items.exampleCN: 年轻读者被那个系列吸引。

items.example: The old judge spoke with quiet gravitas.
items.exampleCN: 老法官说话带着一种沉静的庄重。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 沉重的；有分量的；严重的

latinEntries.meaning: to be heavy, to press down

definition_zh: 空中的；航空的；空气的；（名词）天线
definition_en: relating to the air or to aircraft, or happening high above the ground; as a noun, a device that receives radio or television signals
core_image: 悬在半空的一根细线：既是空气，也是捕捉电波的天线
scene: 清晨的山谷里，摄影师的飞行器缓缓升空，镜头俯瞰着尚未醒来的村庄。 The small drone took an aerial photograph of the valley at sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 aerial 是「空中的、从空中拍摄的」（第 1 个义项：与空气或空中有关）；句意为小型无人机在日出时拍下了山谷的鸟瞰照片。画面中可辨识：飞行器、山谷、晨雾。

pos.zh: 空中的；航空的；空气的
天线

collocations.zh: 鸟瞰；从空中看到的景象

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 aerial 加 -ly 构成，义为「在空中；通过航空方式」
由 aerial 加 -ist 构成，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人

senses.title: Existing in or relating to the air
senses.titleCN: 空气的；存在于空气中的
senses.definition: relating to the air or existing in it
senses.definitionCN: 与空气有关或存在于空气中的
senses.example: Aerial moisture turned the morning air into a thick mist.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的水汽让清晨的空气变成了浓雾。
senses.why: Aer is the Greek word for air, and this adjective simply points to that element.
senses.whyCN: aer 是希腊语里表示「空气」的词，这个形容词直接指向这种元素。

senses.title: High above the ground
senses.titleCN: 高悬空中的；在空中发生的
senses.definition: happening or situated high above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 发生在地面上方高处的，或位于高处的
senses.example: An aerial cableway carried the tourists across the gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条空中索道把游客送过了峡谷。
senses.why: The same air becomes height: what is aerial is up there, away from the ground.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「空气」义进一步变成高度：aerial 的东西就在上方，远离地面。

senses.title: Done from or by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航空的；从飞机上进行的
senses.definition: carried out from an aircraft, especially for photography or survey
senses.definitionCN: 从飞机上实施的，尤指摄影或勘测
senses.example: Aerial surveys mapped the damage after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，航空勘测绘制了受灾范围。
senses.why: Once the word moved from air to aircraft, work done in the sky became aerial work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从「空气」转向「飞机」，在空中完成的作业就成了 aerial 的工作。

senses.title: A device that receives signals
senses.definition: a metal device, often on a roof, that sends or receives radio and television signals
senses.definitionCN: 常装在屋顶、用于收发广播和电视信号的金属装置
senses.example: He climbed onto the roof to fix the aerial.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬上屋顶去修那根天线。
senses.why: An antenna stands up in the air to catch waves, so English reused the air word for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 天线竖立在空气中捕捉电波，于是英语干脆用「空气」这个词来称呼这个物件。

senses.title: Growing above the ground: aerial roots
senses.definition: of a plant part, growing above the ground rather than in the soil
senses.definitionCN: 指植物器官长在地面之上而非土壤之中的
senses.example: Orchids use aerial roots to absorb moisture from the humid air.
senses.exampleCN: 兰花用气生根从湿润的空气中吸收水分。
senses.why: Botany keeps the literal sense: the root lives in the air, not in the soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了最字面的意思：这种根生活在空气里，而不是土壤里。

intro.en: Aerial is built on the Greek word for air and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: aerial 建立在希腊语表示「空气」的词上，经由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun aer meant 'air, mist, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 名词 aer 意为「空气、雾气、低层大气」。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer as 'air' and used it in both everyday and scientific writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer 表示「空气」，日常写作与科学写作中都在使用。

items.en: The adjective aerius meant 'of the air' and supplied the stem behind the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 aerius 意为「空气的」，为英语这个词提供了词干。

items.en: Aerial is recorded in the sixteenth century, first describing things in or of the air.
items.cn: aerial 于十六世纪见于记录，最初描述存在于空气中或与空气有关的事物。

items.en: In the twentieth century the noun aerial was applied to the antenna raised into the air for radio and television.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，名词 aerial 被用来指为收音机和电视竖在空中的天线。

note.en: The first group gathers words on the same air root or resembling aerial in spelling; the second gathers things that are airborne, overhead, or used to catch signals.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「空气」词根构成的词以及与 aerial 拼写相近的词；第二组收升空的、头顶上的或用于接收信号的事物。

entries.definition: To expose something to air or to force air into it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使暴露于空气；向……充气」，与 aerial 同出希腊语「空气」词根。

entries.definition: The nest of a bird of prey, built high on a cliff or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猛禽筑在高处岩壁上的巢」；只是拼写与 aerial 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A performer who works high above the ground, such as a trapeze artist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人，由 aerial 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: Carried in the air, or flying after leaving the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升空的；在空中的」，强调已经离开地面。

entries.definition: Above a person's head; in the sky directly above.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，只强调相对位置，不涉及航空。

entries.definition: A device that sends or receives radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天线」，与 aerial 的名词义项所指同类物件。

normalIntro.en: Aerial can be recalled through its air root, its suffix, and its everyday collocations.
normalIntro.cn: aerial 可以通过「空气」词根、后缀以及常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Aer means air and -ial makes an adjective, so aerial is simply 'of the air'.
normal.cn: aer 意为「空气」，-ial 构成形容词，aerial 就是「空气的」。

normal.en: An aerial view is a view from the air, which fixes the adjective in a familiar phrase.
normal.cn: aerial view 是「从空中看到的景象」，这个常见搭配能固定形容词义。

normal.en: The noun aerial is the antenna that stands up in the air to catch waves.
normal.cn: 名词 aerial 就是竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

normal.en: Aerialist adds -ist to the same word and names a person who performs in the air.
normal.cn: aerialist 加 -ist，指在空中表演的人。

normal.en: Aerate and aerobic share the same air root, so the family can be learned together.
normal.cn: aerate 与 aerobic 共享同一「空气」词根，可以整族一起记。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire hanging above a valley, catching mist on one side and signals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线悬在山谷上方，一边接住雾气，一边接收信号。

abstract.en: Think of a camera lifting off the ground: the higher it goes, the more the view deserves the name aerial.
abstract.cn: 想象相机离开地面升空：升得越高，眼前的景象越配得上 aerial 这个名字。

abstract.en: Link the word to wind on your face: air is the element behind every sense.
abstract.cn: 把这个词和风吹在脸上的感觉联系起来：空气是它所有义项背后的元素。

examples.en: The drone captured an aerial view of the flooded valley.
examples.cn: 无人机拍下了被洪水淹没的山谷鸟瞰图。

examples.en: He replaced the rusty television aerial on the roof.
examples.cn: 他更换了屋顶上生锈的电视天线。

examples.en: From the ridge, the village looked like a patch of colour in a green sea.
examples.cn: 从山脊望去，村庄像绿色海洋中的一小片色彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱瑞尔」——爱（ai）上空气，瑞（ri）尔（al）把它挂在高处，正好是悬在半空的细线。

root: 希腊语 aēr（转写为 aer）意为「空气」，拉丁语 aerius 是其形容词形式「空气的」，英语 aerial 由此而来，后缀 -ial 表示「与……有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from the element air, rise into the sky, move to aircraft, and end with two concrete objects: the antenna and the air root.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「空气」这一元素出发，升到空中，转向航空，最后落到两个具体物件：天线与气生根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line suspended in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根悬在空中的细线

branches.en: The literal element: what belongs to the air.
branches.cn: 本义：属于空气的事物。

branches.en: Height above the ground, where the air is.
branches.cn: 高度：位于地面之上的空中。

branches.en: Work done from aircraft in the sky.
branches.cn: 从飞机上进行的作业。

branches.en: The antenna that stands in the air to catch waves.
branches.cn: 竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

branches.en: The plant root that lives in humid air.
branches.cn: 生长在湿润空气中的植物根。

intro.en: Aerial is built from a Greek air root plus a Latin adjective ending, and its family is easy to map.
intro.cn: aerial 由希腊语「空气」词根加拉丁语形容词词尾构成，词族容易梳理。

latinIntro.en: Latin took aer from Greek and formed aerius 'of the air'; English borrowed the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 aer，并构成 aerius「空气的」；英语借用了这个形容词。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the source of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是整个词族的来源。
aerius 在英语中变成了 aerial。

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；宜人的；和蔼可亲的；赞同的；可接受的
definition_en: pleasant and enjoyable, or willing to accept something
core_image: 一阵让人愿意点头的微风，既不刺人也不沉闷
scene: 午后的小院里，微风穿过树荫，茶香淡淡地散开。 The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
sceneCN: 这里 agreeable 是「宜人的」（第 1 个义项：令人感到舒适愉快的）；句意为这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。图中可辨识物件：小院、树荫、茶杯。

pos.zh: 形容词：令人愉快的；宜人的；赞同的；可接受的

derivatives.zh: 由 agreeable 加 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地；令人愉快地」
由 agreeable 加 -ness 构成，义为「宜人；随和」
由 dis- 加 agreeable 构成，义为「令人不快的；难相处的」

senses.title: Pleasant in weather or setting
senses.definition: pleasantly mild and comfortable, especially of weather or a place
senses.definitionCN: 温和舒适、令人惬意的，尤指天气或场所
senses.example: The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。
senses.why: Agreeable comes from 'pleasing'; a climate that pleases the body is agreeable in the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: agreeable 出自「讨喜」；让身体感到舒服的气候，就是最古老意义上的 agreeable。

senses.title: Easy to be with
senses.definition: friendly and easy to get along with, so that others enjoy one's company
senses.definitionCN: 友善随和、容易相处，别人乐于与之相伴
senses.example: She has an agreeable manner that puts guests at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 她举止和蔼可亲，让客人感到自在。
senses.why: A person who pleases others is agreeable; the word moves from air and food to manners.
senses.whyCN: 讨人喜欢的人就是 agreeable；这个词从空气与食物转移到了举止。

senses.title: Willing to accept
senses.definition: willing to agree to a suggestion or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 愿意同意某项建议或安排
senses.example: They were agreeable to a short delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他们愿意接受短暂的延期。
senses.why: What is agreeable finds favor with you; to be agreeable to a plan is to let it find favor.
senses.whyCN: 合意之物会在你这里得到认可；对一项计划 be agreeable，就是让它获得认可。

senses.title: Acceptable as terms
senses.titleCN: 可接受的；合意的（条件、方案）
senses.definition: satisfactory enough for all concerned to accept, as of terms or a compromise
senses.definitionCN: 足够令人满意、各方都能接受，如条件或折中方案
senses.example: The two sides reached a mutually agreeable compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 双方达成了彼此都能接受的折中方案。
senses.why: In bargaining, what pleases both parties is exactly the agreeable solution.
senses.whyCN: 在谈判中，让双方都满意的东西，正是一项「合意」的解决办法。

senses.title: A welcome experience
senses.definition: giving pleasure or satisfaction, as of an experience, surprise, or piece of news
senses.definitionCN: 带来愉悦或满足，如一段经历、一个惊喜或一条消息
senses.example: An agreeable surprise awaited them at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口有一个令人愉快的惊喜等着他们。
senses.why: Anything that arrives welcome and pleasing earns the same adjective, whether weather, person or news.
senses.whyCN: 任何到来时受欢迎、令人愉悦的东西，都得到同一个形容词，无论是天气、人还是消息。

intro.en: Agreeable is the adjective of 'pleasing', built from the same Latin root as agree.
intro.cn: agreeable 是「讨喜」的形容词，与 agree 出自同一个拉丁词根。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome, and it also gave grateful and gratitude.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」，也生出 grateful 与 gratitude。

items.en: Ad gratum meant 'to one's liking', the phrase behind the whole agree family.
items.cn: ad gratum 意为「合某人的意」，是整个 agree 词族背后的短语。

items.en: Old French agreable described something pleasing or acceptable to a person.
items.cn: 古法语 agreable 形容令人满意、可以接受的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for weather, manners, and things that find favor.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用来形容天气、举止以及讨人喜欢的事物。

items.en: The sense of 'willing to agree' became common in the phrase be agreeable to.
items.cn: 「愿意同意」之义在 be agreeable to 这一说法中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agree family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what pleases or suits.
note.cn: 形近组收 agree 词族；近义组收表示讨喜与适宜的词。

entries.definition: To share an opinion or accept a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；赞成」，指看法相同或接受提议。

entries.definition: The noun for consent, harmony, or a formal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意；一致；协议」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a pleasant way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「愉快地；令人愉快地」。

entries.definition: Giving a feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的」，指带来享受或满足感。

entries.definition: Friendly and pleasant in disposition, easy to like.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」，指性情友善、容易让人喜欢。

entries.definition: Satisfactory enough to be allowed or agreed to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的」，指足以被允许或同意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to the suffix 'can be', to pleasant weather and to a guest one would invite again.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与表示「能够」的词尾、宜人的天气以及愿意再请一次的客人联系起来。

normal.en: AGREEABLE holds agree: anything you can agree to is pleasing.
normal.cn: agreeable 里藏着 agree：你能接受的东西，必是合意的。

normal.en: The suffix -able means 'can be', so agreeable is 'can be agreed with'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 意为「能够」，所以 agreeable 就是「能够与之合意的」。

normal.en: Picture a mild afternoon that makes everyone nod in comfort.
normal.cn: 想象一个温和的午后，人人都舒服得点头。

normal.en: An agreeable guest is one you would gladly invite a second time.
normal.cn: agreeable 的客人，是你乐意再请一次的人。

normal.en: Weather, manners and terms can all be agreeable: the word fits whatever pleases.
normal.cn: 天气、举止、条件都可以是 agreeable：凡是合意的，这个词都用得上。

abstract.en: To be agreeable is to make room for others to agree.
abstract.cn: 令人愉快，就是给别人留出同意的空间。

abstract.en: The word joins comfort of body to ease of company.
abstract.cn: 这个词把身体的舒适与人际的自在连在一起。

abstract.en: A compromise becomes agreeable when both sides can breathe.
abstract.cn: 当双方都能松一口气时，折中方案才变得合意。

examples.en: The weather was unusually agreeable for a long walk.
examples.cn: 这样的天气对长途散步来说格外宜人。

examples.en: She has an agreeable manner that puts guests at ease.
examples.cn: 她举止和蔼可亲，让客人感到自在。

examples.en: They were agreeable to a short delay.
examples.cn: 他们愿意接受短暂的延期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿哥，瑞宝」：阿哥捧出瑞宝，人人都觉得讨喜。

root: 拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的）经 ad gratum「合意」与古法语 agreable 进入英语，-able 表示「能够」，整体意为「能够合人心意的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers pleasant weather, easy company, willingness to accept, acceptable terms and welcome experiences.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖宜人的天气、随和的相处、愿意接受、可接受的条件以及令人愉快的经历。

core.en: PLEASING ENOUGH TO ACCEPT
core.cn: 合意到可以接受

branches.en: weather that pleases the body
branches.cn: 让身体舒服的天气

branches.en: a manner that pleases others
branches.cn: 讨人喜欢的举止

branches.en: a mind willing to accept
branches.cn: 愿意接受的心思

branches.en: terms both sides can accept
branches.cn: 双方都能接受的条件

branches.en: an experience that arrives welcome
branches.cn: 到来时受欢迎的经历

intro.en: Agreeable is agree plus -able, and its negative and adverb forms are built the same way.
intro.cn: agreeable 是 agree 加 -able，它的否定形式与副词形式也按同样方式构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base gratus 'pleasing' also yields grateful and gratitude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 gratus「讨喜的」也生出了 grateful 与 gratitude。

items.meaning: in a pleasant or willing manner

items.example: Her agreeableness made the work easier.
items.exampleCN: 她的随和让工作轻松了许多。

items.meaning: unpleasant or hard to get along with
items.example: The room had a disagreeable smell.
items.exampleCN: 房间里有股令人不快的气味。

items.example: He spoke disagreeably to the clerk.
items.exampleCN: 他没好气地对店员说话。

items.example: They signed the agreement in June.
items.exampleCN: 他们在六月签署了协议。

items.meaning: to share an opinion or accept
items.example: Do you agree with this plan?

items.meaning: the tendency to be pleasing and easy to agree with
items.example: His agreeability won over the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 他的随和赢得了整个团队。

令人不快的；不知感激的

definition_zh: 富裕的；富足的；（地区）高档的；丰富的
definition_en: having a lot of money and a high standard of living; plentiful or abundant
core_image: 水源源不断流进来的样子：钱与资源充盈
scene: 河岸边的山坡上，新盖的房子一栋接一栋，花园里种着整齐的树。 The affluent suburb has large houses, private schools, and quiet streets.
sceneCN: 这里 affluent 是「富裕的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财、生活水准高）；句意为这个富裕的郊区有大房子、私立学校和安静的街道。画面中可辨识：山坡住宅、花园、安静的街道。

pos.zh: 富裕的；富足的；丰富的
富裕人群（the affluent）

derivatives.zh: 由 affluent 去掉词尾加 -ence 构成，义为「富裕；丰裕」
由 affluent 加 -ly 构成，义为「富裕地；丰足地」
由 affluent 与 influenza 缩合而成，指过度追求物质带来的「富裕病」，属非正式用词

senses.title: Having plenty of money
senses.definition: having a great deal of money and a high standard of living
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财、生活水准很高
senses.example: The affluent couple donated a large sum to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 这对富裕的夫妇向图书馆捐了一大笔钱。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to flow toward, and the image is resources flowing in without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「流向」，意象是资源不停地流进来。

senses.title: Of a place: wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: of an area or neighbourhood, inhabited by wealthy people and offering expensive services
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或街区住着富裕人群、提供昂贵服务
senses.example: They moved to an affluent suburb with a private school nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到了一个附近有私立学校的富裕郊区。
senses.why: Wealth spreads across a map: when many rich households cluster, the place itself is called affluent.
senses.whyCN: 财富会铺到地图上：当许多富裕家庭聚集，这个地方本身就被称为 affluent。

senses.title: Existing in abundance
senses.definition: present in large quantities; plentiful, used especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 大量存在的、充裕的，尤用于正式书面语
senses.example: The valley had affluent supplies of water and timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷拥有充裕的水源和木材。
senses.why: The original sense was simply flowing plentifully, before money narrowed the word in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思只是「大量流动」，在日常生活里才被钱的意义收窄。

senses.title: Flowing freely, in older use
senses.definition: flowing freely or in abundance, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 自由地或大量地流动，这一义项较古老，现今罕用
senses.example: The old poem describes an affluent stream that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗描写一条永不干涸的丰沛溪流。
senses.why: Before it named money, the word described water moving in quantity; that literal sense survives mainly in old texts.
senses.whyCN: 在指钱之前，这个词描述的是大量流动的水；这一字面义主要残留在旧文本里。

intro.en: Affluent is built on a Latin verb for flowing, and wealth was originally pictured as a flow of resources.
intro.cn: affluent 建立在拉丁语表示「流动」的动词上，财富最初被想象成资源的流动。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow', and it also gave English fluent and fluid.
items.cn: fluere 意为「流动」，它也给了英语 fluent 与 fluid。

items.en: Affluere meant 'to flow to, to flow in abundance', built with ad- and fluere.
items.cn: affluere 意为「流向、大量涌入」，由 ad- 与 fluere 构成。

items.en: Affluentia named abundance and the flow of wealth or supplies.
items.cn: affluentia 指丰裕，以及财富或物资的流入。

items.en: English first used affluent for flowing abundantly, then for people with abundant means.
items.cn: 英语最初用 affluent 表示「大量流动」，后来才指拥有丰裕资财的人。

items.en: The wealth sense became dominant, while the literal water sense retreated to older texts.
items.cn: 财富义成为主流，字面的水流义退回到旧文本中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'flow' root; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「流动」词根的一族词；近义组收表示财富与富足生活的词。

entries.definition: A state of having a lot of money and material goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕；丰裕」，是 affluent 的名词形式。

entries.definition: Able to speak or write a language easily and smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流利的」，与 affluent 同出拉丁语 fluere「流动」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers flow together, or a coming together of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汇流处；汇集」，同样来自 fluere「流动」。

entries.definition: Having a large amount of money, property, or valuable things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有的」，与 affluent 义项一几乎同义，更直白。

entries.definition: Successful and financially strong, especially of a person or region.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「繁荣的；兴旺的」，侧重发展与成功，而非单纯拥有钱财。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live comfortably.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的；日子好过的」，程度比 affluent 温和。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts, more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的；大量的」，对应义项三，但不含财富义。

normalIntro.en: Affluent is anchored by the root flu, which means flow, and by the picture of money flowing in.
normalIntro.cn: affluent 可以靠表示「流动」的词根 flu，以及钱不断流入的画面来记。

normal.en: Flu means flow, and affluere means to flow toward, so affluent is 'flowing in with resources'.
normal.cn: flu 意为「流动」，affluere 意为「流向」，所以 affluent 就是「资源源源流入」。

normal.en: Affluence is the noun for the state, and affluently is the adverb.
normal.cn: affluence 是表示状态的名词，affluently 是副词。

normal.en: An affluent suburb is a place where wealthy households cluster.
normal.cn: affluent suburb 是富裕家庭聚集的地方。

normal.en: Fluent and fluid share the same root, which keeps the flow image in view.
normal.cn: fluent 与 fluid 共享同一词根，让「流动」的意象始终可见。

normal.en: The phrase the affluent treats the adjective as a collective noun.
normal.cn: 「the affluent」这个说法把形容词当作集合名词使用。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running past a house and never running dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币组成的河从房前流过，永不干涸。

abstract.en: Think of a garden where the sprinkler is always on and the soil is always dark with water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，喷头一直开着，土壤总是被水浸得发黑。

abstract.en: See wealth as a current rather than a pile: what matters is how much keeps arriving.
abstract.cn: 把财富看成水流而不是堆叠：重要的是有多少在不断到来。

examples.en: The affluent neighbourhood has its own marina and tennis club.
examples.cn: 这个富裕的街区有自己的游艇码头和网球俱乐部。

examples.en: Affluent families often spend more on tutoring than on holidays.
examples.cn: 富裕家庭花在辅导上的钱常常比花在度假上的更多。

examples.en: The river ran clear after the spring rains.
examples.cn: 春雨过后，河水清澈地流着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗伦特」——阿（a）弗（fu）伦（lun）特（te），钱像水一样不断流进来，日子就富裕了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「流入、丰沛」，其名词 affluentia 指丰裕；英语先指「大量流动」，后专指富裕。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as water flowing in abundance, then narrows to money, then widens again to rich places and plentiful supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指水大量流动，后收窄为钱财，再扩展为富裕地区与充裕物资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: resources flowing in like a stream
core.cn: 核心意象：资源像溪流一样不断流入

branches.en: Money flowing into a household.
branches.cn: 钱财流入家庭。

branches.en: Wealth written across a whole district.
branches.cn: 财富铺展在整个街区。

branches.en: Supplies present in large quantity.
branches.cn: 大量存在的物资。

branches.en: The old literal sense of water flowing freely.
branches.cn: 水流自由流动的古老字面义。

branches.en: Abundance in money and abundance in goods.
branches.cn: 钱财的丰裕与物资的丰裕。

intro.en: Affluent is a prefix plus the Latin root for flow, with a family that spreads across several everyday words.
intro.cn: affluent 是前缀加拉丁语「流动」词根，其词族分布在好几个日常词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fluere made affluere, and fluentia supplied the noun affluence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fluere 构成 affluere，fluentia 则提供了名词 affluence。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fluere is the root of affluent and fluent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 是 affluent 与 fluent 的词根。

definition_zh: 容纳；为……提供住处；适应；迁就；顾及；调解
definition_en: to provide enough space or lodging for someone, or to adjust so that different needs can fit together
core_image: 把房间的尺寸调到刚好装下所有人，谁也不必挤在门外
scene: 会议室里椅子一圈圈加到最后几乎贴着墙，组织者还在数人头。 The hall was built to accommodate six hundred people, and every seat was taken.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodate 指容纳（第 1 个义项：在空间或数量上容纳）；句意为大厅按容纳六百人设计，而每个座位都坐满了。

pos.zh: 动词：容纳；提供住处；适应；迁就；顾及；调解

collocations.zh: 接待客人；为客人提供住处

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「住处；调节；和解」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的；随和的」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有适应力的；调节的」
由 accommodating 加 -ly 构成，义为「随和地；通融地」

senses.title: To hold a number of people
senses.definition: to provide enough room for a number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 为一群人或一批物品提供足够的空间
senses.example: The stadium can accommodate forty thousand spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座体育场能容纳四万名观众。
senses.why: Latin accommodare meant to make a thing fit a measure, so the first sense is simply a room that fits its crowd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accommodare 意为「使某物合于尺度」，因此第一个义项就是「装得下人群的空间」。

senses.title: To give someone lodging
senses.definition: to provide a room or place to stay for a guest, traveller or group
senses.definitionCN: 为客人、旅客或团体提供房间或住处
senses.example: The family accommodated three students during the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间这家人接待了三名学生住宿。
senses.why: A room is the most concrete kind of space that fits a person, so lodging grew naturally from the idea of making room.
senses.whyCN: 房间是最具体的一种「装得下人」的空间，因此「提供住处」自然地从「腾出空间」发展而来。

senses.title: To adjust to a new condition
senses.definition: to change oneself or a system so that it works in new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变自身或系统，使其在新条件下正常运作
senses.example: The eye accommodates to darkness within a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛在几分钟内就能适应黑暗。
senses.why: The fitting is no longer spatial: an organism or a system reshapes itself until it matches the new measure.
senses.whyCN: 这种「合于尺度」不再是空间上的：生物或系统重新调整自身，直到与新尺度相合。

senses.title: To oblige someone
senses.definition: to do what someone wants in order to help or please them
senses.definitionCN: 为了帮助或取悦某人而按他的意愿行事
senses.example: The manager accommodated her request for a later shift.
senses.exampleCN: 经理通融了她晚班的要求。
senses.why: When the measure is another person, fitting means bending your own schedule to their shape.
senses.whyCN: 当尺度变成了另一个人，合于尺度就意味着把自己的安排弯向对方的形状。

senses.title: To take different needs into account
senses.definition: to include the needs or views of several people or groups in a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在计划中纳入若干人或群体的需要与看法
senses.example: The design accommodates both wheelchair users and cyclists.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计同时顾及轮椅使用者与骑行者的需要。
senses.why: One room must now fit several shapes at once, so the verb shifts from making space to balancing claims.
senses.whyCN: 同一个空间要同时装下几种形状，于是这个动词从「腾出空间」转为「平衡各种诉求」。

senses.title: To reconcile two claims
senses.definition: to bring two ideas or accounts into agreement without destroying either
senses.definitionCN: 使两种观点或说法达成一致，而不破坏其中任何一方
senses.example: The report accommodates the findings of both research teams.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告调和了两个研究团队的结论。
senses.why: Mediation is fitting at a higher level: two accounts are adjusted until they occupy the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 调解是更高层次的「合于尺度」：两种说法被调整到能同处一个框架。

intro.en: Accommodate comes from a Latin verb meaning to fit a thing to a measure. From fitting a room to fitting a person, it widened into adjustment and reconciliation.
intro.cn: accommodate 来自一个意为「使某物合于尺度」的拉丁动词。从「装下空间」到「配合他人」，它的含义扩展为适应与调和。

items.en: Hotels, halls and stadiums advertise how many guests they can accommodate, and the verb has become a plain statement of capacity.
items.cn: 旅馆、礼堂与体育场都宣传自己能容纳多少客人，这个动词已成为对容量的平实陈述。

items.en: Optics borrowed the word for the eye, and accommodation named the lens adjusting to the distance of an object.
items.cn: 光学借用了这个词来描述眼睛，accommodation 指晶状体对物体距离所作的调节。

items.en: The phrase accommodate oneself to a situation fixed the modern sense of adjusting to circumstances.
items.cn: 短语 accommodate oneself to a situation 固定了现代「适应环境」的含义。

items.en: Accommodare joined ad- toward with commodare to make suitable, and meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: accommodare 由 ad-「朝向」与 commodare「使适合」组成，意为「使一物合于另一物」。

items.en: Commodus meant fitting or convenient, built from com- together and modus measure, so the root picture is a thing cut to the right size.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合适的；方便的」，由 com-「共同」与 modus「尺度」构成，词根画面就是按合适的尺寸裁好的一件东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the measure root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for holding, housing and adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同出「尺度」词根的词；近义组收表示容纳、住宿与调整的动词。

entries.definition: A room or place to stay, or the act of adjusting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处；调节；和解」。

entries.definition: Willing to help or agree with others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的；随和的」。

entries.definition: Able to adjust to different conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有适应力的」。

entries.definition: Roomy and comfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽敞舒适的」，同出 commodus。

entries.definition: A product that can be bought and sold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商品」，同出 commodus。

entries.definition: To provide a place for someone to live.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为……提供住所」，与住宿义最接近。

entries.definition: To have space for a number of people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳」，与容量义最接近。

entries.definition: To change in order to suit new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应；改编」，侧重改变自身。

entries.definition: To change slightly so as to fit better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整；调节」，侧重小幅修正。

entries.definition: To do something as a favour for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「帮忙；施恩于」，与通融义相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of measuring a room until every guest fits inside.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「把房间量了又量，直到每位客人都装得下」这一画面。

normal.en: Accommodate contains the word mode: to find the right mode for each person.
normal.cn: accommodate 里藏着 mode：为每个人找到合适的模式。

normal.en: Picture a hotel clerk moving beds until every guest has a room.
normal.cn: 想象旅馆前台不断挪动床位，直到每位客人都有一间房。

normal.en: A hall that can accommodate six hundred people has been measured for six hundred chairs.
normal.cn: 能容纳六百人的大厅，是按六百把椅子量过的。

normal.en: To accommodate a request is to cut your plan to the shape of the asker.
normal.cn: 满足一个请求，就是把自己的计划裁成请求者的形状。

normal.en: The eye accommodates by changing its lens, not its mind.
normal.cn: 眼睛靠改变晶状体来调节，而不是改变想法。

abstract.en: Picture a carpenter shaving a door until it closes without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠把门刨了又刨，直到它关上时没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Every sense fits one thing to another: a crowd to a hall, a guest to a bed, a plan to a need.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在让一物合于另一物：人群合于大厅、客人合于床、计划合于需要。

abstract.en: The legal and diplomatic sense fits two claims into one frame without breaking either.
abstract.cn: 法律与外交的义项，是把两种主张装进同一个框架，而不弄坏任何一方。

examples.en: The new hall can accommodate up to eight hundred guests.
examples.cn: 新礼堂最多可容纳八百位客人。

examples.en: The hotel accommodated us in a larger room when our flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误时，旅馆把我们安排进了一间更大的房间。

examples.en: Good managers accommodate different working styles.
examples.cn: 优秀的管理者会顾及不同的工作方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄康莫得特」——前台把空房间量了又量，正好装下所有人

root: 拉丁语 commodus「合适的」← com-「共同」+ modus「尺度」→ commodare「使适合」→ accommodare「使合于」→ 英语 accommodate。核心是「按尺度裁好」：装得下人群、提供住处、适应环境、迁就请求、顾及多方、调和主张、通融钱款、调节晶状体。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses make room: for people, for guests, for difference, for another's wish, for a detail, and for a disagreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都是「腾出空间」：给人、给客人、给差异、给他人的意愿、给细节，以及给分歧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room measured and cut to fit everyone inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个量好尺寸、裁到刚好装下所有人的房间。

branches.en: THE ROOM: space enough for people or things.
branches.cn: 容纳线：容得下人或物的空间。

branches.en: THE LODGING: a bed for the night.
branches.cn: 住宿线：过夜的一张床。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENCE: one adjusts to another condition.
branches.cn: 适应线：向另一种条件调整。

branches.en: THE WISH: one gives way to another's preference.
branches.cn: 迁就线：顺从他人的偏好。

branches.en: THE RECONCILIATION: details and disputes are fitted together.
branches.cn: 协调线：细节与分歧被拼合到一起。

intro.en: Accommodate is built on the Latin noun for measure, and its family covers nouns, adjectives and adverbs of adjustment.
intro.cn: accommodate 建立在拉丁语「尺度」名词之上，其词族涵盖表示调节的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is modus, commodus, commodare and accommodare.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 modus、commodus、commodare 与 accommodare。

items.example: It appears as ac- before c.
items.exampleCN: 在 c 之前它写作 ac-。

items.example: It gives English mode and moderate.
items.exampleCN: 它产生英语的 mode 与 moderate。
它和 modus 组成 commodus。

items.example: It is the source of commodious.
It is the direct source of accommodate.
items.exampleCN: 它是 accommodate 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 负担得起的；价格合理的；买得起的
definition_en: cheap enough that most people can pay for it; within someone's financial reach
core_image: 标价牌落在口袋能承受的范围之内
scene: 社区中心贴出通知，说新开的诊所提供价格低廉的检查服务。 The clinic offers affordable care for families without insurance.
sceneCN: 这里 affordable 是「负担得起的、价格合理的」（第 1 个义项：费用低到普通人能支付）；句意为这家诊所为自己没有保险的家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。画面中可辨识：社区通知、诊所门口、排队的人。

pos.zh: 负担得起的；价格合理的；买得起的

derivatives.zh: 由 affordable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性；价格可承受程度」
由 affordable 加 -ly 构成，义为「以负担得起的方式；价格合理地」
由 un- 加 affordable 构成，义为「负担不起的；过于昂贵的」

senses.title: Cheap enough to be paid for
senses.definition: having a price low enough that ordinary people can pay it
senses.definitionCN: 价格低到普通人能够支付
senses.example: The clinic offers affordable care for families without insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为自己没有保险的家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns afford into a question of possibility: can your means carry this price?
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把 afford 变成可能性的问题：你的财力能承担这个价格吗？

senses.title: Reasonable in cost relative to value
senses.definition: having a cost that is reasonable in relation to what you receive
senses.definitionCN: 相对所得而言成本合理的
senses.example: For a small car, it is an affordable option with low running costs.
senses.exampleCN: 作为小型车，它的价格合理，使用成本也低。
senses.why: Affordability is not only about being poor: a thing can be affordable because its price matches its value.
senses.whyCN: 可负担性不只关乎钱少：一件东西也可以因为价格与价值相称而显得划算。

senses.title: Of housing: within reach of ordinary incomes
senses.definition: of housing or services, priced so that people with ordinary incomes can obtain them
senses.definitionCN: 指住房或服务定价使普通收入者也能获得
senses.example: The city promised to build more affordable housing near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府承诺在车站附近建造更多经济适用住房。
senses.why: In policy language, affordable names a target, not a compliment: a price a normal salary can actually cover.
senses.whyCN: 在政策语言里，affordable 指一个目标而不是赞美：普通工资确实能覆盖的价格。

intro.en: Affordable is afford plus a Latin-derived suffix, and the word became prominent with housing and health care policy.
intro.cn: affordable 是 afford 加一个源自拉丁语的后缀，随着住房与医疗政策而变得常用。

items.en: The native verb behind afford meant to further or accomplish something.
items.cn: afford 背后的本族动词意为推进或完成某事。

items.en: The verb settled into the sense of having means for something.
items.cn: 这个动词逐渐固定为「有财力做某事」。

items.en: The suffix -abilis meant 'that can be done', and it reached English as -able through French.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 意为「可以被……的」，经法语以 -able 形式进入英语。

items.en: Affordable appears as a regular derivative meaning 'able to be afforded'.
items.cn: affordable 作为规则派生词出现，意为「负担得起的」。

items.en: Housing and health care debates made affordable a standard policy word in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 住房与医疗的讨论使 affordable 在二十世纪成为标准的政策用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about low and reasonable prices.
note.cn: 形近组收本词自己的词族；近义组收表示低价与价格合理的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to have enough money or means for something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「负担得起；提供」，是 affordable 的原词。

entries.definition: The extent to which something can be afforded by ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性」，由 affordable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that is within people's financial reach.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以负担得起的方式」，由 affordable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Costing little money, though sometimes suggesting poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「便宜的」，但常暗含质量不佳，不如 affordable 中性。

entries.definition: Not costing much money, used to avoid the negative tone of cheap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不贵的」，比 cheap 更中性，常用于商品描述。

entries.definition: Fairly priced and not too expensive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「价格公道的；合理的」，侧重价格与价值相称。

entries.definition: Good value because it saves money in use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「经济实惠的」，侧重长期使用省钱，而不只是标价低。

normalIntro.en: Affordable is simply afford plus -able, and the suffix turns an ability into a price judgement.
normalIntro.cn: affordable 就是 afford 加 -able，这个后缀把「能力」变成了对价格的判断。

normal.en: Break it as afford plus able: able to be afforded.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 afford 加 able：能够被负担得起。

normal.en: Affordability is the noun, and it is the word used in housing reports.
normal.cn: affordability 是名词，也是住房报告里常用的词。

normal.en: Affordably is the adverb, as in affordably priced.
normal.cn: affordably 是副词，如 affordably priced 表示「定价合理」。

normal.en: Unaffordable is its opposite, formed with un-.
normal.cn: unaffordable 是它的反义，由 un- 构成。

normal.en: In policy, affordable housing means housing a normal income can cover.
normal.cn: 在政策里，affordable housing 指普通收入能覆盖的住房。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag that fits inside a wallet without tearing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签正好能放进钱包，而不会把钱包撑破。

abstract.en: Think of a door handle placed low enough for a child to reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门把手装得足够低，孩子也够得到。

abstract.en: See affordability as a bridge between what something costs and what someone earns.
abstract.cn: 把可负担性看成标价与收入之间的一座桥。

examples.en: The city needs more affordable housing near public transport.
examples.cn: 这座城市需要在公共交通附近建造更多经济适用住房。

examples.en: They found an affordable option that still included breakfast.
examples.cn: 他们找到一个价格合理、还包含早餐的选择。

examples.en: The queue outside the clinic stretched around the block.
examples.cn: 诊所外的队伍一直排到了街角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福德伯」——阿（a）福（fu）德（de）伯（bo），有福的人手头宽裕，什么都买得起。

root: 由本族词 afford「负担得起」加后缀 -able「可以被……的」构成；-able 源自拉丁语 -abilis，经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts from a simple price test, then adds the idea of fair value, and finally becomes a housing-policy label.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从简单的价格测试出发，再加入「划算」的意思，最后成为住房政策的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag that fits inside a wallet
core.cn: 核心意象：一张能放进钱包的价签

branches.en: A price ordinary people can pay.
branches.cn: 普通人付得起的价格。

branches.en: A cost that matches what you receive.
branches.cn: 与所得相称的成本。

branches.en: A policy label for housing within normal incomes.
branches.cn: 指普通收入可以覆盖的住房政策标签。

branches.en: Cheap enough and fair enough at the same time.
branches.cn: 既足够便宜，又足够公道。

branches.en: Fair pricing turned into a public standard.
branches.cn: 公道定价转化为一项公共标准。

intro.en: Affordable is a native verb plus a borrowed suffix, a common pattern in modern English.
intro.cn: affordable 是本族动词加外来后缀，这是现代英语常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin -abilis by way of French, while the stem afford is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -able 经法语来自拉丁语 -abilis，而词干 afford 属于日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in a way that can be

definition_zh: 毗连；紧挨着；附加
definition_en: to be next to and often touching something; to attach something as an addition
core_image: 两块地皮在地图上共用一条细线
scene: 那块空地紧挨着学校操场，只隔着一道铁丝网。 The empty lot adjoined the school playground, separated only by a wire fence.
sceneCN: 这里 adjoin 指与…毗连（第 1 个义项：紧挨着）；句意为空地紧挨着学校操场，只隔一道铁丝网。

pos.zh: 毗连；紧挨着；附加

derivatives.zh: 由 adjoin 加 -ing 构成，义为「毗连的」
同族形容词，义为「邻近的」
同族名词，义为「邻近、毗连」

senses.title: To be next to
senses.definition: to be next to and usually touch something
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，通常还与之接触
senses.example: Their farm adjoins the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的农场紧挨着那条河。
senses.why: The verb is positional: two pieces of land share an edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是位置性的：两块土地共享一条边。

senses.title: To attach as an addition
senses.definition: to attach or add something to another thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附加到另一物上
senses.example: A small chapel was adjoined to the old church.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小礼拜堂被附建在旧教堂旁。
senses.why: The older sense is joining, and English kept it for physical attachments.
senses.whyCN: 更早的义项就是「连接」，英语把它保留给实体附着。

intro.en: adjoin came through French from a Latin verb that simply meant to join to, and it still keeps that literal force.
intro.cn: adjoin 经法语来自一个意思就是「连接上去」的拉丁动词，至今仍保留这种字面力量。

items.en: Jungere meant to join or yoke, the source of junction and conjunction.
items.cn: jungere 意为连接、套轭，是 junction 与 conjunction 的来源。

items.en: With ad-, it meant to join one thing to another.
items.cn: 加上 ad- 后，意为把一样东西连接到另一样上。

items.en: French carried the verb forward as ajoindre, to join or to be next to.
items.cn: 法语把它传成 ajoindre，意为连接或紧挨。

items.en: English adopted it for land and buildings that touch.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入，用于相接的土地与建筑。

items.en: The word stayed formal and mostly appears in descriptions of property.
items.cn: 这个词保持正式，主要出现在对地产的描述里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the joining root; the near-meaning group is other verbs of touching or bordering.
note.cn: 形近组共享「连接」这个词根；近义组是其他表示接触或接壤的动词。

entries.definition: Next to or sharing a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「邻近的」。

entries.definition: Touching or next to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毗连的」。

entries.definition: A joining together, or a word that joins clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连接；连词」，与 adjoin 同根。

entries.definition: To share a border with a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与…接壤」，多用于国家与地区。

entries.definition: To be in physical contact with something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接触」，强调碰到。

entries.definition: To join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「连接」，强调建立联系。

normalIntro.en: The hooks reduce the word to its join root, then put it back on a map.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词还原成「连接」这个词根，再把它放回地图上。

normal.en: Jungere means to join, and ad- means to, so adjoin is to join on.
normal.cn: jungere 意为「连接」，ad- 意为「向」，所以 adjoin 就是「接到上面」。

normal.en: The commonest use is about land: a lot adjoins a playground.
normal.cn: 最常见的用法是关于土地：一块地紧挨着操场。

normal.en: Adjoining rooms share a wall and are often connected by a door.
normal.cn: adjoining rooms 共享一道墙，常有一扇门相通。

normal.en: The verb is formal; in speech people usually say next to.
normal.cn: 这个动词偏正式；口语里人们通常说 next to。

normal.en: It shares the root of junction and conjunction, which all involve joining.
normal.cn: 它与 junction、conjunction 同根，都跟「连接」有关。

abstract.en: Two plots sharing one thin line on a map.
abstract.cn: 地图上两块地共享一条细线。

abstract.en: A chapel built against an older wall.
abstract.cn: 一座贴着旧墙建起的小礼拜堂。

abstract.en: A door that connects two rooms without a corridor.
abstract.cn: 一扇不经走廊、直接连通两个房间的门。

examples.en: The garden adjoins the neighbour's wall.
examples.cn: 花园紧挨着邻居家的墙。

examples.en: Two adjoining rooms were turned into one.
examples.cn: 两个相连的房间被合并成一个。

examples.en: A garage adjoins the house.
examples.cn: 车库与房子相连。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额乔因」——额头挨着乔因，两个人紧靠在一起

root: 经古法语 ajoindre 来自拉丁语 adjungere「连接到」，由 ad-「向」与 jungere「连接」构成；本义是把东西接上去，后来主要用于土地、房屋彼此毗连。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: land or buildings touching, and an addition attached to something.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：土地或房屋彼此相接，以及把某物附建到另一物上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two plots of land sharing one thin line on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上两块土地共享一条细线。

branches.en: THE RIVER: the farm stops where the water begins.
branches.cn: 河线：农场在水开始的地方结束。

branches.en: THE FENCE: the lot and the playground share wire.
branches.cn: 铁丝网线：空地与操场共享同一道铁丝网。

branches.en: THE CHAPEL: an addition is built against an older wall.
branches.cn: 礼拜堂线：一个附加部分贴着旧墙建起。

branches.en: THE GARAGE: a new structure joins the house.
branches.cn: 车库线：一座新建筑接到房子上。

branches.en: THE JOINT: every use turns on one thing meeting another.
branches.cn: 接合线：每一种用法都归结为一样东西与另一样接上。

intro.en: The Latin verb jungere, to join, took the prefix ad- and passed through French into English as adjoin.
intro.cn: 拉丁动词 jungere「连接」加上前缀 ad-，经法语进入英语，成为 adjoin。

latinIntro.en: jungere and adjungere are attested; ajoindre is the French link, and the endings are English.
latinIntro.cn: jungere 与 adjungere 都有文献可证；ajoindre 是法语中间环节，词尾属于英语。

items.example: It directs the joining towards a neighbour.
items.exampleCN: 它把「连接」指向相邻的一方。

items.example: It is the joining root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一族里「连接」的词根。

items.example: It is the direct Latin source.
It is the short English cousin of jungere.
items.exampleCN: 它是 jungere 在英语里的短亲。
它构成 junction 与 conjunction。

derivatives.zh: 由 adjoin 加 -ing 构成，义为「毗连的」
同族形容词，义为「邻近的」
同族名词，义为「邻近、毗连」

definition_zh: 对手；敌手；敌人；（法庭上的）对方
definition_en: a person or group that opposes another in a contest, conflict, or legal case
core_image: 两个人隔着棋盘对坐，目光都盯着对方的王
scene: 赛前新闻发布会上，两队教练都刻意避免提到对方的名字。 The champion faced a determined adversary in the final round.
sceneCN: 这里 adversary 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：比赛中的对方）；句意为冠军在最后一轮遇到一个顽强的对手。

pos.zh: 对手；敌手；敌人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」
由 adversarial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以对抗方式」
由 adversarial 加 -ness 构成，义为「对抗性」

senses.title: An opponent in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that competes against another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方竞争的人或队伍
senses.example: The champion faced a determined adversary in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军在最后一轮遇到一个顽强的对手。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'turned against', so an adversary is someone whose face is turned toward you in opposition.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「转向对立面」，所以对手就是面对面与你相对的人。

senses.title: An enemy in a conflict
senses.definition: a person or group actively hostile in a struggle or war
senses.definitionCN: 在斗争或战争中主动敌对的个人或群体
senses.example: The two countries had been adversaries for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家几十年来一直是敌手。
senses.why: Contest and conflict share the same structure: two sides turned against each other.
senses.whyCN: 竞争与冲突结构相同：两方彼此转向对立。

senses.title: The opposing side in a legal case
senses.definition: the opposing party in a legal proceeding, often used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 法律程序中的对方当事人，常置于名词前作定语
senses.example: The case was decided in an adversary proceeding.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案件在对抗式程序中得到裁决。
senses.why: Law treats the two parties as opponents facing each other across the courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 法律把双方当事人当作在法庭两端相对的对手。

intro.en: Adversary comes from a Latin word for an opponent, built on the verb 'to turn'.
intro.cn: adversary 出自一个表示「对手」的拉丁词，其基础是「转」这个动词。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」。

items.en: Adversus meant turned toward or turned against.
items.cn: adversus 意为转向、转为对立。

items.en: Adversarius named a person who stands opposed to another.
items.cn: adversarius 指站在他人对立面的人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from a contestant to an enemy and to the opposing party in law.
items.cn: 词义从比赛对手扩展到敌人，再扩展到法律上的对方当事人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'turn against' root; the near-meaning group gathers opponents and enemies.
note.cn: 形近组共享「转向对立」词根；近义组收对手与敌人。

entries.definition: Unfavourable or harmful; literally turned against.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不利的」，字面即「转为对立」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A difficult or unlucky situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逆境」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Characterized by opposition or conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「对抗性的」，由本词加 -ial 构成。

entries.definition: Strongly disliking something; from the same verb of turning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反感的」，出自同一「转」动词，属同根但用法不同。

entries.definition: A person who competes against another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对手」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: A person or group competing for the same goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「竞争者」，强调争夺同一目标。

entries.definition: A person or group actively hostile to another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敌人」，敌意最强。

entries.definition: An enemy, used mainly in literary or formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敌人」，多用于文学或正式文本。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'turn against' root and the contest, war, and courtroom settings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的「转向对立」词根，以及比赛、战争与法庭三个场景。

normal.en: Vertere means to turn, so an adversary is someone turned against you.
normal.cn: vertere 意为转，所以对手就是转向你对立面的人。

normal.en: Adverse and adversity share the same root: what is turned against you.
normal.cn: adverse 与 adversity 同根：转向你、与你作对之物。

normal.en: In a contest, the adversary is the other side of the board.
normal.cn: 在比赛中，对手就是棋盘对面的那一方。

normal.en: In law, the adversary is the opposing party across the courtroom.
normal.cn: 在法律中，对手就是法庭另一端的对方当事人。

normal.en: A worthy adversary is one who makes the contest better.
normal.cn: a worthy adversary 指让比赛更精彩的对手。

abstract.en: Two chairs facing each other across a chessboard.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子隔着棋盘相对而放。

abstract.en: Two flags on opposite hills.
abstract.cn: 两面旗子插在对望的山头。

abstract.en: A door that opens only toward one person.
abstract.cn: 一扇只朝一个人方向打开的门。

examples.en: She defeated a much younger adversary in the final.
examples.cn: 她在决赛中击败了一个年轻得多的对手。

examples.en: The two leaders had been adversaries for years.
examples.cn: 这两位领导人多年来一直是敌手。

examples.en: The lawyer studied the adversary's arguments.
examples.cn: 律师研究了对方的论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃瑟里」——阿德把椅子转向对面，与沃瑟里对峙

root: 源自拉丁语 adversarius「对手」，出自 adversus「转向、对立」，而 adversus 又出自 vertere「转」；古法语 adversaire 带入英语。核心是「转过身来与你相对」，由此发展出「比赛对手」「敌人」「法庭上的对方」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the contestant, the enemy, and the opposing party in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：比赛对手、敌人、法律上的对方当事人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people sit across a board, each watching the other's king.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔着棋盘对坐，各自盯着对方的王。

branches.en: THE BOARD: the other player competes for the same win.
branches.cn: 棋盘线：另一位玩家争夺同一场胜利。

branches.en: THE WAR: hostility turns the contest into enmity.
branches.cn: 战争线：敌意把竞争变成敌对。

branches.en: THE COURT: two parties face each other in law.
branches.cn: 法庭线：双方在法律上彼此相对。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: opposition is formal in both game and law.
branches.cn: 结构线：无论游戏还是法律，对立都是形式化的。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: whether enemy or opposing party, the figure is defined from the opposite side.
branches.cn: 对方线：无论敌人还是对方当事人，这个身份都由对立面定义。

intro.en: Adversary is built on the Latin verb 'to turn', with direction and a person suffix.
intro.cn: adversary 建立在拉丁语「转」这个动词上，加上方向与表示人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, adversus and adversarius are recorded, so the family is well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere、adversus 与 adversarius 均有记录，这一词族文献充分。

items.example: It directs the turning toward someone.
It is the direct source of adversary.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adversary 的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」
由 adversarial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以对抗方式」
由 adversarial 加 -ness 构成，义为「对抗性」

definition_zh: 搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动；鼓动
definition_en: to shake or stir something, to make someone anxious, or to campaign publicly for a cause
core_image: 用长柄勺不停搅动一锅浓汤，让沉底的东西翻上来
scene: 厨房里，厨师用长柄勺快速搅动锅里的浓汤。 She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle at the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 agitate 是「搅动」（第 1 个义项：反复摇动或搅拌液体与混合物）；句意为她搅动汤，免得奶油沉在锅底。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、长柄勺、灶台。

pos.zh: 动词：搅动；摇动；使焦虑；煽动

derivatives.zh: 由 agitate 加 -ion 构成，义为「搅动；焦虑；鼓动」
由 agitate 加 -or 构成，义为「搅动器；鼓动者」
由 agitate 加 -ed 构成，义为「焦虑不安的」
由 agitate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人不安的；搅动的」

senses.title: To stir a liquid
senses.definition: to shake or stir a liquid or mixture so that its parts move and mix
senses.definitionCN: 反复摇动或搅拌液体或混合物，使各部分流动混合
senses.example: She agitated the soup so the cream would not settle.
senses.exampleCN: 她搅动汤，免得奶油沉下去。
senses.why: Latin agitare was the frequentative of agere 'to do, drive', so it meant 'to keep driving something about'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agitare 是 agere「做、驱动」的反复形式，意为「反复把某物来回驱赶」。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to disturb someone's calm and make them feel nervous or upset
senses.definitionCN: 打破某人的平静，使其感到紧张或烦躁
senses.example: The strange phone calls agitated her all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那些奇怪的电话让她整晚心神不宁。
senses.why: If liquid can be stirred, so can the mind: the same word describes thoughts kept from settling.
senses.whyCN: 既然液体能被搅动，心也能被搅动：同一个词描述无法平静下来的思绪。

senses.title: To campaign for a cause
senses.definition: to argue publicly and persistently for a political or social change
senses.definitionCN: 公开而持续地为某项政治或社会变革奔走呼吁
senses.example: The group agitated for cleaner water in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体为山谷里更清洁的水源奔走呼吁。
senses.why: Public opinion is another liquid: the campaigner keeps stirring it until it moves.
senses.whyCN: 舆论也是一种液体：鼓动者不断搅动它，直到它流动起来。

senses.title: To stir up debate
senses.definition: to provoke discussion, unrest, or strong feeling among a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中激起讨论、骚动或强烈情绪
senses.example: The question agitated the whole committee for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题在委员会里激起了数周的争论。
senses.why: A stirred pot does not stay still; a stirred group of people will not either.
senses.whyCN: 被搅动的锅不会静止；被搅动的人群也不会。

senses.title: To shake a container
senses.definition: to shake a vessel or device so that its contents move
senses.definitionCN: 摇动容器或装置，使里面的东西运动
senses.example: Agitate the bottle before pouring the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 倒药之前先摇匀瓶子。
senses.why: This is the physical core at its simplest: a closed vessel is made to move so its contents follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的物理核心：让封闭的容器运动起来，里面的东西随之而动。

intro.en: Agitate is the Latin verb 'to keep driving about', a frequentative built on agere.
intro.cn: agitate 是拉丁语「反复驱动」的动词，由 agere 的反复形式构成。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion, the base of act, agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，是 act、agent、agenda 的词基。

items.en: The frequentative agitare meant to keep driving or shaking something, to set it in repeated motion.
items.cn: 反复动词 agitare 意为「反复驱动或摇动某物」，使其持续运动。

items.en: The participle agitatus described something shaken or kept in motion, and also a troubled mind.
items.cn: 分词 agitatus 描述被摇动、处于运动中的事物，也指不安的心。

items.en: English borrowed the word first for physical stirring and shaking.
items.cn: 英语最初借入这个词，用来指物理上的搅动与摇动。

items.en: By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries it also meant to stir up feeling or to campaign politically.
items.cn: 到十八、十九世纪，它又指搅动情绪或在政治上进行鼓动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of stirring and campaigning.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示搅动与鼓动的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for stirring, nervous unrest, or public campaigning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅动；焦躁；鼓动」，兼指物理与情绪、政治三方面。

entries.definition: A device that stirs, or a person who campaigns for change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅拌器；鼓动者」，既指搅动的装置，也指推动变革的人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning nervous, upset, or physically shaken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑不安的；被摇动的」。

entries.definition: To move a spoon or other object around in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「搅拌」，指用勺等物在液体中转动。

entries.definition: To interrupt someone's peace or make them worried.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰；使不安」，指打断平静或让人担忧。

entries.definition: To take part in organized activity aimed at a political or social goal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开展运动；奔走」，指为政治或社会目标组织活动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to a stirring spoon, a restless mind and a speaker working up a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与搅拌的勺子、不安的心以及煽动人群的演讲者联系起来。

normal.en: AGITATE contains ag- 'do' and -itate, a suffix of repeated action: to keep doing something to a liquid.
normal.cn: agitate 含 ag-「做」与表示反复动作的 -itate：对液体反复做某个动作。

normal.en: Picture a spoon going round and round in a pot of soup.
normal.cn: 想象一把勺子在汤锅里一圈圈地转。

normal.en: A shaken bottle of medicine must be agitated before use.
normal.cn: 药瓶用前要摇匀，这个动作就是 agitate。

normal.en: When worry stirs your thoughts, you feel agitated.
normal.cn: 当忧虑搅动思绪时，你就感到心神不宁。

normal.en: A campaigner agitates public opinion the way a spoon agitates soup.
normal.cn: 鼓动者搅动舆论，就像勺子搅动汤。

abstract.en: To agitate is to refuse to let something settle.
abstract.cn: 搅动，就是不让某样东西沉淀下来。

abstract.en: The same motion calms soup and unsettles people.
abstract.cn: 同一种运动，能让汤均匀，也能让人心不安。

abstract.en: Political agitation is a mind kept deliberately in motion.
abstract.cn: 政治鼓动，就是一颗被有意搅动的心。

examples.en: Agitate the paint before you open the can.
examples.cn: 打开漆罐之前先把它摇匀。

examples.en: The waiting crowd grew agitated as the hours passed.
examples.cn: 随着时间一小时小时过去，等候的人群越来越焦躁。

examples.en: For years the villagers agitated for a new road.
examples.cn: 多年来村民们一直为新修一条路而奔走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿吉，忒特」：阿吉忒特别，总爱搅动锅里的汤，也搅动大家的情绪。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的反复形式 agitare（反复驱动、摇动），过去分词 agitatus 进入英语，核心意象是「反复搅动」，由物及心，再到政治鼓动。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with physical stirring, extends to a disturbed mind, and ends with public campaigning and debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从物理搅动开始，延伸到被搅乱的心，最后落在公开鼓动与争论上。

core.en: KEEP SOMETHING IN MOTION
core.cn: 让某物持续运动

branches.en: a liquid stirred in a pot
branches.cn: 锅里被搅动的液体

branches.en: a closed vessel shaken
branches.cn: 被摇动的封闭容器

branches.en: a mind kept from settling
branches.cn: 无法平静的心

branches.en: opinion stirred for a cause
branches.cn: 为某项事业被搅动的舆论

branches.en: a group stirred into debate
branches.cn: 被搅起争论的一群人

intro.en: Agitate is the frequentative member of the ag- family, marking repeated or vigorous action.
intro.cn: agitate 是 ag- 词族中的反复成员，标记反复或剧烈的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere 'do' plus the frequentative suffix -itare produced agitare, the source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere「做」加上反复后缀 -itare 造出 agitare，成为这一组的源头。

items.example: His agitation showed in his shaking hands.
items.exampleCN: 他双手发抖，显出内心的焦躁。

items.meaning: a device or person that stirs
items.example: The washing machine has a central agitator.
items.exampleCN: 这台洗衣机中央有一个搅拌器。

items.example: The agitated patient could not sit still.
It was an agitating piece of news.
items.exampleCN: 那是一条令人不安的消息。
这份传单纯粹是鼓动性的。

items.meaning: political art or writing meant to stir support
items.meaningCN: 鼓动宣传；政治宣传作品
items.example: The play was dismissed as agitprop.
items.exampleCN: 这部剧被讥为政治宣传。

items.meaning: in a nervous or shaken manner
items.example: She paced agitatedly by the door.
items.exampleCN: 她在门口焦躁地来回踱步。

items.example: He remained unagitated during the storm.

latinEntries.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被摇动的；被搅动的；不安的

definition_zh: 社会的；整个社会层面的；涉及社会结构与集体规范的
definition_en: relating to society as a whole, especially to its structures, norms and collective effects

scene: 这里指「社会的」。 The new subway line created societal pressure on housing and on the old neighbourhoods near the station.
sceneCN: 此处指「影响整个社会层面、而非只落在个别人身上的压力」（第 1 个义项：属于社会整体而非个体的）；句意是新地铁线给车站周边的住房与老街坊带来了整体性的压力。可辨识物件：地铁入口、施工围挡、租房广告、居委会窗口。

pos.zh: 社会的；整个社会层面的（正式、学术语域）
涉及社会结构或集体规范的

senses.title: Relating to society as a whole
senses.definition: relating to society considered as one whole rather than to any single person in it
senses.definitionCN: 把社会视为一个整体而非其中任何个人
senses.example: The new subway line created societal pressure on housing and on the old neighbourhoods near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 新地铁线给车站周边的住房与老街坊带来了整体性的压力。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun society into an adjective, and the whole-society reading is what distinguishes it from social.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -al 把名词 society 变成形容词，而「整体社会」这一读法正是它与 social 的区别。

senses.title: Relating to social structure
senses.definition: concerning the way a society is divided into classes, roles and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 涉及社会如何划分为阶层、角色与制度
senses.example: Societal divisions along income lines shaped who could buy into the new district.
senses.exampleCN: 按收入划出的社会分层决定了谁买得起新城区。
senses.why: When writers needed to point at structure rather than at friendly interaction, they reached for this more formal adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当作者要指结构而非友好交往时，就会用这个更正式的形容词。

senses.title: Relating to shared norms
senses.definition: concerning the rules and expectations that a community holds in common
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一个共同体共同持有的规则与期待
senses.example: Changing societal norms made it normal for fathers to take parental leave.
senses.exampleCN: 社会规范的变化使父亲休育儿假成为常态。
senses.why: Norms belong to no single individual, so the adjective naturally describes what is held collectively.
senses.whyCN: 规范不属于任何个人，因此这个形容词自然用来描述集体持有的东西。

senses.title: Relating to public consequences
senses.definition: concerning effects that spread beyond one household to the public at large
senses.definitionCN: 涉及超出单个家庭、扩散到公众的影响
senses.example: The factory closure had societal costs that no single owner had to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭带来的社会代价，没有任何一个业主需要独自承担。
senses.why: The word is used to name costs and benefits that fall on everyone, which is why it often appears with pressure and cost.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用来指落在所有人身上的代价与收益，因此常与「压力」「代价」一类词连用。

senses.title: Relating to group relations
senses.definition: concerning relations between groups within a society, such as regions or generations
senses.definitionCN: 涉及社会内部群体之间的关系，如地区之间或代际之间
senses.example: Societal tension between the coast and the inland towns shaped the election.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海与内陆城镇之间的社会紧张影响了这次选举。
senses.why: Group relations are a whole-society topic, so the adjective covers what happens between groups as well as inside them.
senses.whyCN: 群体关系属于整体社会议题，因此这个形容词既涵盖群体内部，也涵盖群体之间。

senses.title: Relating to collective cost
senses.definition: concerning a burden that is shared by many households rather than carried by one
senses.definitionCN: 涉及由许多家庭分摊而非由一家承担的负担
senses.example: Elder care became a societal burden once the birth rate fell.
senses.exampleCN: 出生率下降后，养老照护成了整个社会的负担。
senses.why: A cost becomes societal when it is pooled, which is the same idea as the public-consequence sense seen from the budget side.
senses.whyCN: 代价一旦被汇集分摊，就成了社会性的；这与「公共后果」义只是从预算角度看的同一件事。

senses.title: Relating to cultural patterns
senses.definition: concerning the habits, rituals and values that a society transmits across generations
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一个社会代代相传的习惯、仪式与价值
senses.example: Societal attitudes toward silence differ sharply between the two regions.
senses.exampleCN: 两个地区对沉默的社会态度差别很大。
senses.why: Culture is carried by a whole society rather than by one speaker, so the adjective fits patterns that outlive individuals.
senses.whyCN: 文化由整个社会承载，而非由某个说话者承载，因此这个形容词适合描述比个人活得久远的模式。

senses.title: Contrasted with the individual
senses.definition: used to mark the level of analysis that stands opposite to personal or individual explanations
senses.definitionCN: 用来标出与个人解释相对的分析层次
senses.example: The study moved from individual choices to societal causes without losing the thread.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究从个人选择转向社会成因，却没有失去线索。
senses.why: Much of social science works by contrast between individual and societal levels, and the adjective was coined to name the second term cleanly.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学大量依靠「个人」与「社会」两个层次的对照，这个形容词正是为了干净地命名后一项而造出的。

intro.en: Societal is an English adjective formed from society with the Latin-derived suffix -al. It entered academic writing as a formal alternative to social. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: societal 是由 society 加拉丁来源的词尾 -al 构成的英语形容词，作为 social 的正式替代形式进入学术写作。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun comes from Latin societas 'association, community', itself from socius 'ally'.
items.cn: 基础名词来自拉丁 societas「联合、共同体」，其词根为 socius「盟友」。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed adjectives of relation in Latin and reached English as -al, as in social and societal.
items.cn: 词尾 -alis 在拉丁语中构成表示关系的形容词，进入英语后作 -al，如 social 与 societal。

items.en: Societal is a modern formation built directly on the English noun rather than inherited as a single Latin word.
items.cn: societal 是直接由英语名词构成的现代形式，并非作为单一拉丁词继承而来。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread in sociology and policy writing because it could mark the whole-society level without the everyday flavour of social.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词在社会学与政策写作中传播开来，因为它能标出整体社会层次，又不带 social 的日常色彩。

items.en: Dictionaries treat societal as formal and often prefer social in ordinary speech; the two words overlap but are not freely interchangeable.
items.cn: 词典把 societal 标为正式用语，日常口语常更倾向 social；两者有重叠，却不能随意互换。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of societal is not precisely established, and estimates for it vary, so no exact year is claimed here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：societal 最早的印刷用例缺乏精确考证，各家估计不一，因此这里不给出确切年份。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that look alike or share the root but point at different levels; group two holds words for what is shared by a group.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近或同根、但指向不同层次的形容词；第二组是指由群体共享之物的词。

entries.definition: The ordinary adjective for interaction, status or public life; it is broader and less formal than societal.
entries.definitionCN: 描述交往、地位或公共生活的日常形容词；比 societal 更宽、更不正式。

entries.definition: Describes a person who enjoys company; it never describes a whole society.
entries.definitionCN: 描述喜欢与人相伴的人，不能描述整个社会。

entries.definition: Describes someone trained into social norms, or something made public; it is a verb form, not a level label.
entries.definitionCN: 描述受过社会规范训练的人或被公有化的事物；它是动词形式，不是层次标签。

entries.definition: Stresses common use or common identity inside a smaller community; societal points at the whole-society level.
entries.definitionCN: 强调较小共同体内部的共用或共同身份；societal 指向整个社会层次。

entries.definition: Means performed or held by a group as a unit; it can apply to a team as easily as to a nation.
entries.definitionCN: 指由群体作为一个单位完成或持有，既可用于团队，也可用于国家。

entries.definition: Relates to the state, services or open access; societal relates to society's structure and norms.
entries.definitionCN: 与国家、公共服务或公开性有关；societal 则与社会结构与规范有关。

entries.definition: Names the arrangement of parts, often economic or institutional; societal is wider and includes norms and culture.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分的排列，常偏经济或制度；societal 更宽，含规范与文化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Society plus -al: the adjective simply means 'of society', with a formal, academic tone.
normal.cn: society 加 -al：这个形容词就是「社会的」，带正式学术语气。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: societal norms, societal pressure, societal change, societal impact.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层次：社会规范、社会压力、社会变化、社会影响。

normal.en: The word is common in sociology and policy writing, where the whole-society level must be named precisely.
normal.cn: 这个词常见于社会学与政策写作，因为那里需要精确命名整体社会层次。

normal.en: It contrasts with individual: individual choices on one side, societal causes on the other.
normal.cn: 它与「个人」相对：一边是个人选择，一边是社会成因。

normal.en: The family runs society, social, socialization and sociologist, all from the same Latin stock.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 society、social、socialization 与 sociologist，均出同一拉丁来源。

abstract.en: Picture a city seen from a tower: the streets are individual lives, the pattern is the societal level.
abstract.cn: 想象从塔上俯瞰城市：街道是个人生活，图案才是社会层次。

abstract.en: Picture a pressure gauge attached not to one pipe but to the whole water system.
abstract.cn: 想象压力表不是接在一根管子上，而是接在整个供水系统上。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that nobody wrote down but every household follows at dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没人写下、却在家家户户饭桌上被遵守的规则。

examples.en: Societal expectations still push young couples toward a house before a child.
examples.cn: 社会期待仍推动年轻夫妇先买房再要孩子。

examples.en: The report separated individual habits from societal causes.
examples.cn: 这份报告把个人习惯与社会成因区分开来。

examples.en: Rising rents became a societal issue rather than a private complaint.
examples.cn: 租金上涨成了社会议题，而不只是私人抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社会的）+ tal（整体）」——把整个社会当成一个整体来看 → 社会层面的

root: societal 由英语名词 society 加拉丁来源词尾 -al 构成；society 经古法语来自拉丁 societas，词根 socius「盟友」。这是现代英语形容词，不是拉丁语固有单词；最早书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one shift of viewpoint: the same town is seen first as a whole, then as structure, norms, public cost, group tension, shared burden, culture and finally as the level opposed to the individual.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一次视角转换：同一座城镇先被看作整体，再被看作结构、规范、公共代价、群体紧张、共同负担、文化，最后被看作与个人相对的层次。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a city seen from a tower, where individual streets add up to one visible pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：从塔上俯瞰的城市，一条条街道汇成一张可见的图案。

branches.en: WHOLE LEVEL: the adjective starts by naming society as one unit.
branches.cn: 整体层次：这个形容词首先把社会当作一个单位来命名。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: divisions of class, role and institution are the skeleton of that unit.
branches.cn: 结构：阶层、角色与制度的划分是这个单位的骨架。

branches.en: NORMS AND TENSION: shared rules hold groups together and also set them against one another.
branches.cn: 规范与紧张：共同规则既把群体维系在一起，也使群体彼此对立。

branches.en: PUBLIC COST: effects and burdens that no single household can carry alone.
branches.cn: 公共代价：没有任何单个家庭能独自承担的影响与负担。

branches.en: CULTURE AND CONTRAST: transmitted patterns outlive individuals, which is why the level is set against the person.
branches.cn: 文化与对照：代代相传的模式比个人活得久，因此这一层次被拿来与个人对照。

intro.en: The adjective is an English noun plus a Latin-derived ending, and its parts are shared with the rest of the society family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是英语名词加拉丁来源词尾构成，其成分与社会词族其他成员共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin societas and the suffix -alis are the two ingredients; English supplied the modern noun base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 societas 与词尾 -alis 是两个原料，现代英语提供了名词基础。

items.example: The root names the associated people.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指联合起来的人。

items.example: The ending makes the noun society.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成名词 society。
社会层面的变化来得很慢。
这个问题根在社会层面。
一位社会学家主持了这项调查。

definition_zh: n. 生物群落（一定生境内相互关联的全部生物）
definition_en: the whole community of living organisms that share a habitat and interact with one another
core_image: 一片浅水里，芦苇、鱼、水鸟和看不见的细菌被同一张网连在一起
scene: 这片湿地里的动植物构成了一个完整的生物群落。 The plants and animals of the wetland form a single biocenosis.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biocenosis 指同一生境内相互关联的全部生物；句意是这片湿地的动植物构成一个完整群落。

pos.zh: 生物群落

senses.title: All the organisms of one habitat
senses.titleCN: 同一生境内的全部生物
senses.definition: the interacting group of plants and animals living together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 在同一地点共同生活的植物与动物的互动集合
senses.example: A pond biocenosis includes reeds, fish, insects and bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘生物群落包括芦苇、鱼类、昆虫和细菌。
senses.why: It was coined in German ecology from bios, life, and koinos, common, for the common living population of a site.
senses.whyCN: 它由德语生态学以 bios（生命）与 koinos（共同）创造，指一处地点共同的生物群体。

senses.title: The living part alone, without its setting
senses.definition: the living community considered separately from the soil, water and climate around it
senses.definitionCN: 把生物群落与周围的土壤、水和气候分开来考虑时的部分
senses.example: In this scheme the biocenosis is the living half and the biotope the physical half.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种划分里，biocenosis 是活的半边，biotope 是物理环境的半边。
senses.why: Ecologists needed a word for the organisms by themselves, because ecosystem names organisms plus their environment.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家需要专指生物本身的词，因为 ecosystem 指生物加环境。

intro.en: Biocenosis is Greek bios, life, plus koinos, common, plus the noun ending -osis.
intro.cn: biocenosis 是希腊语 bios（生命）加 koinos（共同），再接名词词尾 -osis。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biography.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biography 的第一构件。

items.en: Koinos means common or shared, as in koine, the common Greek.
items.cn: koinos 意为共同、共有，如 koine（共通希腊语）。

items.en: The German ecologist Karl Mobius names the community of organisms.
items.cn: 德国生态学家 Karl Mobius 为这一生物共同体命名。

items.en: The term passes into French and English ecology.
items.cn: 该术语进入法语与英语生态学。

items.en: Biocenosis becomes a standard unit of field study.
items.cn: biocenosis 成为野外研究的标准单位。

items.en: Modern texts often prefer community, but the word survives in ecology.
items.cn: 现代文献多用 community，但该词仍在生态学中沿用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bio- front; the near-meaning group separates the living community from its physical setting and from the larger system that includes both.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bio- 开头；近义组把生物群落与物理环境、以及包含二者的更大系统区分开。

entries.definition: An older spelling of the same term.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的较早拼写。

entries.definition: Relating to a community of organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物群落有关的。

entries.definition: The physical space occupied by a community.
entries.definitionCN: 群落所占据的物理空间。

entries.definition: The origin of living things from living things.
entries.definitionCN: 生物由生物产生。

entries.definition: Organisms and their surroundings as one system.
entries.definitionCN: 生物与其环境构成的整体系统。

entries.definition: All the species living in one area.
entries.definitionCN: 同一地区内的全部物种。

entries.definition: The natural home of a species.
entries.definitionCN: 物种的天然居所。

entries.definition: All living things on the planet together.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上全部生物的整体。

normalIntro.en: Bios is life and koinos is common, so a biocenosis is the common life of one place.
normalIntro.cn: bios 是生命，koinos 是共同，所以 biocenosis 是一处地方共同的生命。

normal.en: Bio- at the front always means life.
normal.cn: 开头的 bio- 永远表示「生命」。

normal.en: Koinos means common, as in the koine Greek of traders.
normal.cn: koinos 意为共同，如商人们通用的 koine 希腊语。

normal.en: Put together: the common life of a habitat.
normal.cn: 合起来：一个生境共同的生命。

normal.en: Reeds, fish, birds and bacteria all belong to one biocenosis.
normal.cn: 芦苇、鱼、鸟和细菌同属一个生物群落。

normal.en: Its physical counterpart is the biotope, the place itself.
normal.cn: 与之相对的物理部分是 biotope，即地点本身。

abstract.en: A net woven out of species.
abstract.cn: 用物种织成的一张网。

abstract.en: One address shared by thousands of lives.
abstract.cn: 成千上万生命共用的同一个地址。

abstract.en: The living half of a landscape.
abstract.cn: 一片景观中「活着」的那一半。

examples.en: The lake biocenosis shifted after the invasive snail arrived.
examples.cn: 入侵螺类到来后，湖泊生物群落发生了变化。
