examples.en: Ecologists map a biocenosis before drawing the boundary of a reserve.
examples.cn: 生态学家先给生物群落绘图，再划定保护区边界。

examples.en: The biotope is the stage and the biocenosis is the cast.
examples.cn: biotope 是舞台，biocenosis 是演员。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio 是「生命」，cenosis 让人想到「共聚一处」——一个地方所有生命共同聚在一起，就是生物群落。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ koinos（共同）+ -osis（状态、过程）

sensesIntro.en: The word names the living cast of a place; the second sense only makes explicit that the stage itself belongs to another term.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指一处地方的「活演员」；第二义只是点明舞台本身属于另一个术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reeds, fish, wading birds and invisible bacteria tied together by one shallow pond
core.cn: 核心意象：芦苇、鱼、涉禽与看不见的细菌，被同一片浅水连在一起

branches.en: Reeds standing in still water.
branches.cn: 立在静水中的芦苇。

branches.en: Bacteria working unseen in the mud.
branches.cn: 在泥中无声工作的细菌。

branches.en: A boundary drawn between life and soil.
branches.cn: 在生命与土壤之间画出的界线。

branches.en: A biotope named separately from its species.
branches.cn: 与物种分开命名的生境。

branches.en: One site split into cast and stage.
branches.cn: 把一处地点分为演员与舞台。

intro.en: Biocenosis is Greek in every part; the list below separates life, commonness and the noun endings that ecology borrows.
intro.cn: biocenosis 各部分都来自希腊语；下面把「生命」「共同」与生态学借用的名词词尾分开。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios is life, koinos is common, and oikos is house, the root of ecology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为生命，koinos 意为共同，oikos 意为家宅，是 ecology 的词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bios 产生 biology 与 biocenosis。
koinos 产生 biocenosis 与 koine。
oikos 产生 ecology 与 economy。

definition_zh: 论战文章；激烈争论；论战
definition_en: a strong written or spoken attack on a position, made to win rather than to understand
core_image: 一篇小册子，页边写满批注，每个句子都像在挥拳
scene: 那本小册子没有数据，只有火气，读起来是一篇论战。 The pamphlet carried no figures, only heat, and read like a polemic from its first page.
sceneCN: 这里 polemic 指论战文章（第 1 个义项：论战文章）；句意为那本小册子没有数据，只有火气，从第一页起就像一篇论战。

pos.zh: 论战文章；激烈争论；论战

senses.title: Written attack
senses.definition: a piece of writing that argues hard against a position
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一立场强硬地展开攻击的文字
senses.example: His polemic against the new tax ran to forty pages.
senses.exampleCN: 他反对新税的那篇论战写了四十页。
senses.why: The word names the piece itself, not the person who wrote it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名文章本身，而不是写文章的人。

senses.title: Spoken attack
senses.definition: a speech or a broadcast that fights a case in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合为某一立场开火的演讲或广播
senses.example: The radio polemic ended with three names read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 那场广播论战以念出三个名字收尾。
senses.why: The mouth can carry a polemic as well as a page.
senses.whyCN: 嘴也能承载论战，不只是纸面。

senses.title: Genre
senses.definition: a style that puts argument before evidence
senses.definitionCN: 把论证放在证据之前的文体
senses.example: The essay is a polemic in form, whatever its footnotes say.
senses.exampleCN: 无论注释怎么写，这篇文章在形式上都是论战。
senses.why: The genre is recognised by its posture, not by its topic.
senses.whyCN: 这个文体靠姿态被认出，不靠题目。

senses.title: Religious polemic
senses.definition: controversy over doctrine conducted in pamphlets and sermons
senses.definitionCN: 用小册子与布道进行的教义争论
senses.example: Seventeenth-century religious polemic was a blood sport.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的宗教论战是一场见血的运动。
senses.why: The oldest home of the word is the pamphlet war.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的家是小册子之战。

senses.title: Political polemic
senses.definition: argument aimed at a party or a policy rather than at a person
senses.definitionCN: 指向一个政党或一项政策、而非某个人的争论
senses.example: The editorial was political polemic dressed as analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇社论是披着分析外衣的政治论战。
senses.why: Politics gave the word its modern audience.
senses.whyCN: 政治给了这个词现代的听众。

senses.title: Against criticism
senses.definition: attack that seeks victory rather than understanding
senses.definitionCN: 追求胜负而非理解的攻击
senses.example: A review asks what a book is; a polemic asks who is right.
senses.exampleCN: 书评问这本书是什么，论战问谁是对的。
senses.why: The difference is the goal, not the temperature.
senses.whyCN: 差别在目的，不在温度。

senses.title: Polemicist's stance
senses.definition: the posture of a writer who treats an opponent as an enemy
senses.definitionCN: 写作者把对手当作敌人的那种姿态
senses.example: The polemicist never lets the other side finish a sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 论战者从不让对方说完一句话。
senses.why: Here the noun describes a role as much as a text.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词既描述文本，也描述角色。

senses.title: Argument as noise
senses.definition: heat without substance, argument performed for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质的火气，演给观众看的争论
senses.example: The panel dissolved into polemic before the first question.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个问题还没问完，讨论组就沦为一团攻讦。
senses.why: The word can dismiss as easily as it can praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能称赞，也一样能打发。

intro.en: Polemic comes from the Greek word for war: an argument imagined as a campaign with a front line.
intro.cn: polemic 来自希腊语的「战争」：争论被想象成一场有前线的战役。

items.en: Polemos meant 'war', the plain noun behind the whole family.
items.cn: polemos 意为「战争」，是整族词背后那个朴素的名称。

items.en: Polemikos meant 'of war, warlike', an adjective for things that fight.
items.cn: polemikos 意为「战争的、好战的」，是形容交战之物的形容词。

items.en: Latin took polemicus for controversial writing, especially in theology.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 polemicus 指争论性的文字，尤其在神学里。

items.en: English borrowed polemic during the pamphlet wars of the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪的小册子之战中借入了 polemic。

items.en: Newspapers and parties later moved the word from doctrine to policy.
items.cn: 报纸与政党后来把这个词从教义移向政策。

note.en: The look-alike group is the polemos family; the near-meaning group separates diatribe, invective, tirade and critique.
note.cn: 形近组是 polemos 词族；近义组把「谩骂」「恶语」「长篇指责」与「评论」分开。

entries.definition: the practice of controversy.
entries.definitionCN: 论战的做法。

entries.definition: of or like a polemic.
entries.definitionCN: 论战性的。

entries.definition: one who writes polemics.
entries.definitionCN: 写论战的人。

entries.definition: in a combative way.
entries.definitionCN: 以好斗的方式。

entries.definition: a long bitter attack.
entries.definitionCN: 漫长而尖刻的攻击。

entries.definition: abusive language.
entries.definitionCN: 辱骂的语言。

entries.definition: a long angry speech.
entries.definitionCN: 长篇愤怒的讲话。

entries.definition: a careful judgement of a work.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品的审慎评判。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a pamphlet whose margins are all fists.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一本页边全是拳头的册子」的画面。

normal.en: Polemic holds polemos, Greek for war: the page is a front line.
normal.cn: polemic 里藏着 polemos（希腊语的战争）：纸面就是前线。

normal.en: Think of a pamphlet with no numbers in it, only heat.
normal.cn: 想象一本没有数字、只有火气的小册子。

normal.en: Po-LE-mic: the stress sits on le, and the word leans forward.
normal.cn: po-LE-mic：重音落在 le，整个词向前倾。

normal.en: Say POH-luh-mik; the flat first syllable is the calm before the attack.
normal.cn: 读成 POH-luh-mik，平的第一音节是攻击前的安静。

normal.en: Pair it with critique: a critique wants to understand, a polemic wants to win.
normal.cn: 把它和 critique 配对：critique 想理解，polemic 想赢。

abstract.en: A polemic is an argument that has decided the answer before the evidence arrives.
abstract.cn: 论战是一个在证据到齐前就已经定了答案的论证。

abstract.en: The word is borrowed from war, which is why it never sounds like a seminar.
abstract.cn: 这个词借自战争，所以它从不像研讨会。

abstract.en: Polemic can be brave or cheap; the word records the fighting, not the worth of it.
abstract.cn: 论战可以是勇敢的，也可以是廉价的；这个词记录战斗，不记录价值。

examples.en: The pamphlet read like a polemic from its first page.
examples.cn: 那本小册子从第一页起就像一篇论战。

examples.en: His polemic against the new tax ran to forty pages.
examples.cn: 他反对新税的那篇论战写了四十页。

examples.en: A review asks what a book is; a polemic asks who is right.
examples.cn: 书评问这本书是什么，论战问谁是对的。

dict_mnemonic.text: pole（杆）+ mic（麦克风）：举着杆子对着麦克风开火，就是「论战」。

root: 希腊语 polemos（战争）与 -ikos（形容词词尾），经拉丁语 polemicus 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one fight in different rooms: a page, a microphone, a genre, a church, a parliament, a review, a writer's posture and a panel that has stopped listening.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一场战斗换在不同的房间：纸面、麦克风、文体、教会、议会、书评、写作者的姿态，以及一个已经不再倾听的讨论组。

core.en: A PAMPHLET WITH FISTS IN THE MARGINS
core.cn: 页边写着拳头的册子

chain: THE ARGUMENT ENDS IN A SCORE

branches.en: A page and a microphone.
branches.cn: 纸面与麦克风。

branches.en: A style that puts argument first.
branches.cn: 把论证放在最前的文体。

branches.en: A church and a parliament.
branches.cn: 教会与议会。

branches.en: The difference from criticism and the writer's stance.
branches.cn: 与批评的差别，以及写作者的姿态。

branches.en: Heat with nothing behind it.
branches.cn: 背后空空的火气。

intro.en: The polemos family is small and warlike: polemic is the fight, polemics is the practice, a polemicist is the fighter.
intro.cn: polemos 词族小而好战：polemic 是那场战斗，polemics 是作战的做法，polemicist 是作战的人。

latinIntro.en: Greek polemos supplies the war, and the ending -ikos, Latin -icus, turns it into an adjective of controversy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 polemos 提供战争，词尾 -ikos（拉丁语 -icus）把它变成争论的形容词。

items.example: The two editors polemicized in public.
items.exampleCN: 两位主编曾在公开场合论战。

definition_zh: 界面设计；设计人与设备或程序之间交互方式的工作
definition_en: the work of shaping how a person meets and operates a device, program or system
core_image: 一台机器的面板上，按钮的大小、顺序与标注被反复调整，直到陌生人不看说明也能按对
scene: 工作台上摊着几张手绘的面板草图，按钮被反复挪动位置，旁边的测试者皱起眉头又松开。 Good interface design lets a first-time user finish the task without reading the manual.
sceneCN: 这里 interface design 指设计人与设备之间交互方式的工作（第 1 个义项：界面设计这项工作）；句意：好的界面设计让第一次使用的人不看说明书就能完成任务。

pos.zh: 界面设计；交互界面设计（作定语）

senses.title: The craft of shaping an interaction
senses.titleCN: 塑造交互方式的这门手艺
senses.definition: the practice of deciding how a person will meet, understand and operate a system
senses.definitionCN: 决定人如何接触、理解并操作一套系统的实践
senses.example: Interface design asks what the user is trying to do before asking what looks good.
senses.exampleCN: 界面设计先问用户想做什么，再问什么好看。
senses.why: a compound of an object and an activity names the activity, so the phrase first denotes the craft.
senses.whyCN: 「对象＋活动」的复合词指活动本身，因此这个短语首先指这门手艺。

senses.title: The visual arrangement of a screen
senses.definition: the layout of controls, text and space on a display
senses.definitionCN: 显示屏上控件、文字与空白的排布
senses.example: The interface design puts the search box where the eye lands first.
senses.exampleCN: 这次界面设计把搜索框放在视线最先落到的位置。
senses.why: users meet a screen before they meet a method, so the phrase often means the arrangement they see.
senses.whyCN: 用户先遇到屏幕，再遇到方法，因此这个短语常指他们看得见的排布。

senses.title: A phase of a product project
senses.titleCN: 产品项目中的一个阶段
senses.definition: the stage between requirements and build when interaction is settled
senses.definitionCN: 需求与开发之间、确定交互方式的阶段
senses.example: Interface design comes before the code freeze, not after it.
senses.exampleCN: 界面设计在代码冻结之前，而不是之后。
senses.why: work that must be finished at a fixed point becomes a named phase of the schedule.
senses.whyCN: 必须在固定节点完成的工作，会变成进度表上有了名字的阶段。

senses.title: A branch of human-computer interaction
senses.titleCN: 人机交互中的一个分支
senses.definition: the research and teaching area that studies how people and machines meet
senses.definitionCN: 研究人与机器如何相遇的研究与教学领域
senses.example: Her doctorate is in interface design, not in graphic art.
senses.exampleCN: 她的博士方向是界面设计，而不是平面艺术。
senses.why: a craft with its own methods and evidence becomes a discipline with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 有了自己的方法与证据的手艺，会变成有名目的学科。

senses.title: Design of physical controls
senses.definition: the arrangement of buttons, dials and labels on a machine or panel
senses.definitionCN: 机器或面板上按钮、旋钮与标注的布置
senses.example: Interface design for a lift panel must work for a hand in gloves.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯面板的界面设计必须让戴手套的手也能操作。
senses.why: the screen is recent, but the problem of a panel a stranger must read is old.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕是晚近的东西，但「陌生人必须读懂的面板」这个问题很古老。

senses.title: Design of a programmatic interface
senses.definition: the shaping of functions, names and data that one program offers another
senses.definitionCN: 一个程序向另一个程序提供的函数、命名与数据的塑造
senses.example: Interface design for the library matters as much as its speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个库的接口设计与其速度同样重要。
senses.why: the word interface also names the seam between programs, and design applies there without any pixels.
senses.whyCN: interface 也指程序之间的接缝，在那里做设计并不涉及任何像素。

senses.title: The usability craft behind a flow
senses.titleCN: 支撑一条任务流程的可用性工艺
senses.definition: the work of ordering steps so a task can be finished with few errors
senses.definitionCN: 安排步骤顺序，使任务能以很少的错误完成
senses.example: Checkout interface design cut abandoned carts by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 结账流程的界面设计让放弃购物车的人少了三分之一。
senses.why: the measure of the craft is whether people finish, so the phrase also names the work aimed at that measure.
senses.whyCN: 这门手艺的衡量标准是人能否完成，因此短语也指为达成该标准所做的工作。

senses.title: The finished design as an artifact
senses.titleCN: 作为成果的界面设计方案
senses.definition: the document or file that specifies the final arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 规定最终排布的文件或图样
senses.example: The engineers built exactly the interface design she handed over.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师完全照她交出的界面设计方案实现。
senses.why: an activity noun routinely stands for its product, and a design handed over is such a product.
senses.whyCN: 活动名词常指其产物，交付出去的设计图就是这样的产物。

intro.en: Interface design joins a Latin preposition, a Latin word for shape, and a Latin verb for marking out. Both halves passed through French before English used them together.
intro.cn: interface design 由一个拉丁介词、一个表示「形状」的拉丁词和一个表示「标画」的拉丁动词组成。两部分都经法语转手，英语才把它们合起来用。

items.en: Latin inter meant between or among, and English kept that sense in the prefix of interface.
items.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，英语在 interface 的前缀里保留了这个意思。

items.en: Latin facies meant form, appearance or outward look, and English face still carries both the bodily and the surface sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 facies 意为「形状、外观」，英语 face 至今兼有「脸」与「表面」两层意思。

items.en: Interface first named a boundary surface where two bodies meet, and only later the meeting point between a person and a machine.
items.cn: interface 最初指两个物体相接的边界面，后来才指人与机器相遇的地方。

items.en: Designare meant to mark out or trace, from signum, a mark; English design kept the sense of a plan marked down before it is made.
items.cn: designare 意为「标画、描出」，来自 signum「标记」；英语 design 保留了「先画好再做」的意思。

items.en: Both interface and design entered English through French forms, which is why their spelling and stress differ from the Latin originals.
items.cn: interface 与 design 都经法语形式进入英语，所以拼写与重音都与拉丁原词不同。

items.en: The full phrase became common with computing, when the seam between person and machine became something a specialist had to plan.
items.cn: 随着计算机普及，人与机器之间的接缝需要专人规划，这个完整短语才流行起来。

note.en: The first group shares the words inside the compound; the second group is the neighbouring design and research fields.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合词内部的词；第二组是相邻的设计与研究领域。

entries.definition: The meeting surface itself; the compound adds the work of deciding its shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指相接的界面本身；复合词加上「决定其形态」的工作。

entries.definition: The part a person actually sees and touches, as opposed to interfaces between programs.
entries.definitionCN: 人实际看见并触碰的部分，与程序之间的接口相对。

entries.definition: The general activity of planning a form; joined to interface it narrows to human interaction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指规划形态的活动；与 interface 组合后收窄为人机交互。

entries.definition: The one who does the work; the phrase names the work, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指做这项工作的人；短语指工作，而不是人。

entries.definition: The design of behaviour and response over time; interface design often concentrates on the surface that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 设计随时间变化的行为与反馈；interface design 常更专注于承载它的表面。

entries.definition: How easily a task is completed; it is the test of interface design rather than the designing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 任务完成的容易程度；它是界面设计的检验标准，而不是设计本身。

entries.definition: The placement of elements on a surface; layout is one outcome of interface design, not the whole craft.
entries.definitionCN: 元素在表面上的摆放；layout 只是界面设计的一个结果，不是全部。

entries.definition: The academic study of people and machines; interface design is its applied craft.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人与机器的学科；interface design 是它的应用手艺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Latin pieces and the real professional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实拉丁构件与真实行业搭配。

normal.en: Inter means between and face means surface, so an interface is the surface between two parties.
normal.cn: inter 表示「之间」，face 表示「表面」，interface 就是两方之间的表面。

normal.en: Design comes from marking out: the designer draws before the builder builds.
normal.cn: design 来自「标画」：设计者先画，建造者再造。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: user interface design, interface design principles, interface design tools.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：用户界面设计、界面设计原则、界面设计工具。

normal.en: The test is behavioural: can a stranger finish without the manual.
normal.cn: 检验标准是行为上的：陌生人能否不看说明书就完成。

normal.en: The phrase has no pixels in its second sense: an interface between two programs is also designed.
normal.cn: 这个短语的另一义与像素无关：两个程序之间的接口同样需要设计。

abstract.en: Picture a doorknob that tells your hand which way to turn before your eyes read anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门把手，在你眼睛读到任何字之前，就先告诉你的手该往哪边转。

abstract.en: Picture a panel whose labels fade as soon as a stranger stops needing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一块面板，陌生人一不需要说明，标注就自动淡去。

abstract.en: Picture a seam between two rooms that has been made wide enough to walk through without noticing.
abstract.cn: 想象两间屋子之间的接缝被做得足够宽，走过去时根本察觉不到。

examples.en: Interface design fails quietly when a button looks like decoration.
examples.cn: 当按钮看起来像装饰时，界面设计就悄悄失败了。

examples.en: They rewrote the interface design after watching five users hesitate.
examples.cn: 看过五位用户犹豫之后，他们重写了界面设计。

examples.en: Interface design for the control room had to survive cold hands and loud noise.
examples.cn: 控制室的界面设计必须经得起手冷和噪声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特（inter）费事（face）第一赛（design）」——人与机器之间那层费事的表面，要第一赛着设计

root: 拉丁 inter「之间」+ facies「形状、外观」→ 英语 interface；拉丁 designare「标画」← signum「标记」→ 法语 → 英语 design；两词在计算机时代合成 interface design。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the craft to the screen layout, the project phase, the research branch, physical panels, program interfaces, the usability work and the delivered plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从手艺出发，走向屏幕排布、项目阶段、研究分支、实体面板、程序接口、可用性工作与交付的方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine panel redrawn again and again until a stranger presses the right button without instructions.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器面板被反复重画，直到陌生人不必看说明就能按对按钮。

branches.en: CRAFT AND USABILITY: the practice of shaping the meeting, and the work of ordering steps so tasks finish.
branches.cn: 手艺与可用性：塑造相遇方式的实践，以及安排步骤使任务完成的工作。

branches.en: VISIBLE SURFACES: a screen layout, and the older physical panel with buttons and labels.
branches.cn: 可见的表面：屏幕排布，以及更古老的、带按钮与标注的实体面板。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER: a phase in the schedule, and the plan handed to builders at its end.
branches.cn: 先后两端：进度表上的一个阶段，以及阶段结束时交给实现者的方案。

branches.en: RESEARCH BRANCH: the academic study of how people and machines meet.
branches.cn: 研究分支：关于人与机器如何相遇的学术研究。

branches.en: PROGRAM SEAM: an interface with no pixels, designed for another program to call.
branches.cn: 程序接缝：没有像素的接口，供另一个程序调用。

intro.en: Interface design is two Latin-derived nouns placed side by side; neither half takes a new affix in the compound.
intro.cn: interface design 是两个拉丁来源名词并置而成；在复合词中，两半都没有新增词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies inter, facies, signum and designare; French supplied the modern shapes of both nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 inter、facies、signum 与 designare；法语提供了两个名词的现代形式。

items.example: The prefix places the surface between two parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个介词把表面放在两方之间。

items.example: The noun supplies the visible side of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供这个词「可见的一面」。

items.example: English kept both the bodily and the surface sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留了「脸」与「表面」两义。

items.example: The mark is what design originally traced.
items.exampleCN: 「标记」正是设计最初要描出的东西。

items.example: The verb joins planning to drawing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把规划与绘制连在一起。

items.structure: design (English noun and verb from French)
items.meaning: a plan or to plan a form
items.example: The word entered English through French dess(e)ign.
items.exampleCN: 这个词经法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The ending names the person who carries out the craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指从事这门手艺的人。

items.example: Designing is the ongoing work behind a finished design.
items.exampleCN: designing 是成品方案背后的持续工作。

definition_zh: 战争；作战；（尤指）进行战争的行为与方式
definition_en: the activity of fighting a war, especially the manner in which armed conflict is conducted
core_image: 泥泞的旷野上，翻倒的辎重车还在冒烟，地平线被火光染红，半埋的头盔露出边缘
scene: 泥泞的旷野上，翻倒的辎重车还在冒烟，地平线被火光染红，半埋的头盔露出边缘。 Modern warfare depends on drones as much as on infantry.
sceneCN: 这里 warfare 指「进行战争的行为与方式」（第 1 个义项：以有组织武装力量交战的整体活动，尤指其打法）；句意为现代战争对无人机的依赖不亚于对步兵的依赖。图中可辨识物件：翻倒的辎重车、升起的烟、被火光染红的地平线、半埋的头盔。

pos.zh: 战争；作战（一般不可数；指某一类作战方式时可加修饰语，如 guerrilla warfare）

derivatives.zh: 战争；打仗（古北法语 werre 出自法兰克语 *werra「混乱、争斗」，语义偏移为「有组织的武装冲突」，与拉丁 bellum 无关）
战士（war 加古法语施事后缀 -eur，经 werreur 进入英语，语义偏移为「上阵作战的人」）
好战的（war 加古英语相似后缀 -lic，语义偏移为「带有战争气息的」）
战时（war 与 time 的英语复合，time 源自古英语 tima「时间」，语义偏移为「战争持续的时期」）
军舰（war 与 ship 的英语复合，ship 源自古英语 scip「船」，语义偏移为「为作战而建的船」）
车费；行程；过活（古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，语义偏移为「出行、旅费、进食」，正是 warfare 后半的来源）

senses.title: The conduct of armed conflict
senses.definition: the activity of fighting with organized armed forces, especially the way it is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 以有组织的武装力量交战这一活动，尤指其进行方式
senses.example: Modern warfare depends on drones as much as on infantry.
senses.exampleCN: 现代战争对无人机的依赖不亚于对步兵的依赖。
senses.why: War can mean the declared state; warfare names the doing of it, so the word describes activity rather than a legal condition.
senses.whyCN: war 可以指宣示的状态，warfare 命名的是「做」这件事，因此它描述活动而非法律状态。

senses.title: A state of war between parties
senses.definition: the condition in which two or more states or factions are openly or formally at war
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个国家或派别公开或正式处于交战之中的状况
senses.example: The two republics drifted into warfare after the border patrols clashed.
senses.exampleCN: 边境巡逻队冲突之后，两个共和国逐渐滑入战争状态。
senses.why: The second element once meant a journey or expedition, so the word can name a whole stretch of hostile going, not only a battle.
senses.whyCN: 后半部分原指旅程或出征，因此这个词可以命名一整段敌对行程，而不只是一场战斗。

senses.title: A named type of war
senses.definition: a labeled mode of fighting, such as conventional, guerrilla, naval, chemical or cyber warfare
senses.definitionCN: 有标签的作战方式，如常规战、游击战、海战、化学战或网络战
senses.example: Guerrilla warfare bogged down the occupying army for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 游击战让占领军陷于泥潭达十年之久。
senses.why: Types branch off naturally because warfare names a manner of fighting, and manners can always be labeled.
senses.whyCN: 类型会自然分出来，因为 warfare 命名的是打法，而打法总能被贴上标签。

senses.title: Military operations taken as a whole
senses.definition: the collective name for campaigns, raids, sieges and patrols conducted by an armed force
senses.definitionCN: 对一支武装力量所进行的战役、突袭、围攻与巡逻的整体称呼
senses.example: The museum's maps record the warfare of an entire campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 馆里的地图记录了整场战役的军事行动。
senses.why: Once many operations are seen together, the mass of them takes the same name as the activity that produced them.
senses.whyCN: 当许多行动被放在一起看时，这一大堆行动就与产生它们的活动同名。

senses.title: Figurative struggle
senses.definition: a hostile contest waged with pressure rather than weapons, as in class warfare or price warfare
senses.definitionCN: 以压力而非武器进行的敌对较量，如阶级对抗或价格战
senses.example: The two chains waged price warfare until smaller shops closed.
senses.exampleCN: 两家连锁店打价格战，直到小店纷纷关门。
senses.why: Any contest that feels like a campaign borrows the word, whether the weapons are prices, laws or insults.
senses.whyCN: 任何感觉像战役的较量都会借用这个词，无论武器是价格、法律还是恶语。

senses.title: The art of war
senses.definition: the study of strategy, logistics and tactics as a disciplined craft
senses.definitionCN: 把战略、后勤与战术当作一门有章法的技艺来研究
senses.example: He studied warfare at the staff college for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在参谋学院学了两年战争艺术。
senses.why: The conduct of war can be taught and examined, so the activity turns into a subject with its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 作战可以被教授与考核，因此这项活动变成一门有自身规则学问。

senses.title: The destruction war leaves behind
senses.definition: the ruin of towns, fields and lives that armed conflict produces, often spoken of as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 武装冲突造成的城镇、田野与生命的毁坏，常被当作一整片来谈论
senses.example: Whole districts still show the scars of that warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 整片城区至今仍留着那场战争造成的伤痕。
senses.why: The object of the word can be the wreckage rather than the fighting, because destruction is what warfare leaves visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的所指可以是废墟而非战斗，因为战争留下的可见之物正是破坏。

senses.title: Open conflict between groups
senses.definition: hostility between gangs, factions or communities, short of a declared war
senses.definitionCN: 帮派、派系或社区之间的敌对，尚未达到宣战程度
senses.example: Police blame gang warfare for the shootings in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把该区的枪击归因于帮派争斗。
senses.why: Where organized groups fight without states, the same word describes the smaller war without any legal claim.
senses.whyCN: 当有组织的群体在没有国家的情况下打斗，同一个词就用来描述这场规模更小的战争，不涉任何法律主张。

intro.en: War comes from a Frankish word of strife, not from Latin bellum, while the second element is Old English faru 'journey, troop'. The compound is native English built on a borrowed first word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: war 来自法兰克语中表示争斗的词，并非拉丁 bellum；后半部分是古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」。整个复合词是英语本土构造，只借了第一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Werra meant 'confusion, strife, discord'; it is a reconstructed form, written with an asterisk because no text records it directly.
items.cn: werra 意为「混乱、争斗、不和」；它属重构形式，写作时加星号，因为没有任何文本直接记录它。

items.en: Old North French took the Frankish word as werre and passed it to English after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古北法语把法兰克语这个词吸收为 werre，并在诺曼定居之后传入英语。

items.en: English spelled it werre and warre before settling on war, and the word never came from Latin bellum.
items.cn: 英语先写作 werre、warre，后来定为 war；这个词从来不出自拉丁 bellum。

items.en: Faru meant 'a journey, an expedition, a troop on the move', and it is the same word that survives in fare.
items.cn: faru 意为「旅程、出征、行进中的队伍」，与今天仍存的 fare 是同一个词。

items.en: The compound of war plus fare named the waging of war, literally a going to war with troops.
items.cn: war 与 fare 的复合词命名「进行战争」，字面就是带着队伍出征。

items.en: Source uncertain (reconstruction and first date): werra is a reconstruction and its deeper origin is source uncertain; the first English use of the compound is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（重构形式与首见年代）：werra 属重构形式，其更早来源属来源不确定；这个复合词在英语中最早的使用只能大致系年。

note.en: Group one holds the two elements that make the compound plus near-identical words built on them, which are often read as if they meant the same thing; group two holds other names for organized fighting.
note.cn: 第一组是构成该复合词的两个部分及其上长出的形近词，常被误读为同义；第二组是有组织交战的其他名称。

entries.definition: The conflict itself or its declared condition; warfare is the conduct, not the declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 指冲突本身或宣示的状态；warfare 指进行方式，而非宣示。

entries.definition: A journey, a passenger's ticket or the price of travel; the element once meant exactly a journey, not a cost.
entries.definitionCN: 指行程、车票或旅费；这一词素原义正是「旅程」，并非「费用」。

entries.definition: Well plus fare, 'the state of faring well'; it is not war plus fare and has nothing to do with fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 由 well 加 fare 构成，意为「过得好」的状态；它不是 war 加 fare，与打仗无关。

entries.definition: The fighter, built on the same war stock with an agent suffix; it names a person, not an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗者，由同一 war 词干加施事后缀构成；它指人，不指活动。

entries.definition: Actual fighting between forces; combat is the clash, whereas warfare is the whole activity and its manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队之间的实际交火；combat 是那一下碰撞，warfare 则是整体活动及其打法。

entries.definition: Any prolonged hostility, from a border skirmish to a trade dispute; it need not involve armies at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何持续的敌对，从边境小规模冲突到贸易争端；可完全不涉及军队。

entries.definition: The official term for acts of war once they begin; it belongs to communiques rather than to description.
entries.definitionCN: 对开战行为的正式称呼；它属于公报语言，而非描写语言。

entries.definition: One engagement between forces; warfare contains many battles and outlives all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队之间的一次交战；warfare 包含许多场战斗，并比它们持续更久。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Werra 'strife' came from Frankish, not from Latin bellum, so war and the Latin words for war are not relatives.
normal.cn: werra「争斗」来自法兰克语，而非拉丁 bellum，因此 war 与拉丁语中表示战争的词并非同族。

normal.en: The second element is Old English faru 'journey, troop', the same word that survives in fare and farewell.
normal.cn: 后半部分是古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，与 fare、farewell 中留存的是同一个词。

normal.en: The compound is a going to war: war plus fare, not war plus a ticket price.
normal.cn: 这个复合词意为出征：war 加 fare，而不是 war 加票价。

normal.en: The family runs war, warrior, warlike, wartime, warship, warfare.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 war、warrior、warlike、wartime、warship、warfare。

normal.en: Collocations label the kinds: guerrilla warfare, chemical warfare, naval warfare, modern warfare.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：游击战、化学战、海战、现代战争。

abstract.en: Picture a column of carts rolling out at dawn, dust rising behind them in one long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一列车队在黎明出发，扬起的尘土在车后拉成长长一条。

abstract.en: Picture a map with red arrows drawn over it, arrows that stop at a river and never resume.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上画着红色箭头，箭头在一条河边停住，再没有继续。

abstract.en: Picture a field of wheat with a single track cut through it, straight as a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一片麦田被一道笔直如尺的车辙从中划开。

examples.en: The manual treats warfare as a craft with rules, not as a series of heroic episodes.
examples.cn: 这本手册把作战当作一门有规则的技艺，而不是一串英雄插曲。

examples.en: Drought and warfare drove the same families across the border in the same season.
examples.cn: 旱灾与战乱在同一个季节把同一批家庭赶过了边境。

examples.en: Economists now speak of warfare between platforms over the same customers.
examples.cn: 经济学家如今谈论平台之间为争夺同一批顾客而展开的战争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「war（打）+ fare（走一趟）」——带着队伍出去打一趟 → 战争、作战；fare 这里是「行程」不是「费用」

root: war 来自古北法语 werre，源自法兰克语 *werra「混乱、争斗」（重构形式），并非拉丁 bellum；-fare 来自古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，与 fare、farewell 同族。warfare 不是 war 加 fare「费用」，而是「出征打仗」。*werra 更早来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one expedition: troops go out to fight, and that going is then read as the conduct itself, a state, a labeled type, the mass of operations, a metaphor, an art, the ruin left, and finally any group's open conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次出征展开：队伍出去作战，这次出行再依次被读作作战本身、战争状态、贴标签的类型、行动的总和、比喻、技艺、留下的废墟，最后是任何群体的公开冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of carts and troops on the move, and the ground behind them already burnt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支车队与队伍正在开拔，身后的地面已经烧过。

branches.en: DOING AND BEING: the activity of fighting and the condition of being at war are one event seen as motion or as state.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：交战的活动与处于战争中的状态，是同一事件被看作运动或状态。

branches.en: MANNER AND MASS: a labeled way of fighting and the sum of all operations both describe how the war is waged.
branches.cn: 方式与总和：有标签的打法与所有行动的总和，都在描述战争如何被进行。

branches.en: METAPHOR AND CRAFT: any hard contest borrows the word, and the real thing can be studied as an art.
branches.cn: 比喻与技艺：任何激烈较量都借用这个词，而真实战争可以被当作技艺来研究。

branches.en: THE WRECKAGE: what remains visible of warfare is the ruin, so the word can name the damage itself.
branches.cn: 废墟：战争可见的遗留就是毁坏，因此这个词也能指破坏本身。

branches.en: SMALLER WAR: groups without states repeat the whole shape at the scale of a street.
branches.cn: 更小的战争：没有国家的群体在街区的规模上重演整个结构。

intro.en: The word is a native compound with a borrowed first element: a Frankish noun of strife, an Old English noun of journey, and a second element that behaves almost like a suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是本土复合词，只有第一个成分是借来的：一个法兰克语「争斗」名词、一个古英语「旅程」名词，以及一个作用近乎后缀的第二成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin kin here: war is Frankish in origin rather than Latin bellum, and fare is Old English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族：war 源自法兰克语而非拉丁 bellum，fare 属古英语，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The asterisk marks a form reconstructed from later evidence.
items.exampleCN: 星号表示这是依据后世材料重构的形式。

items.example: The French form is the direct bridge to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语形式是通往英语的直接桥梁。

items.example: English shortened the borrowed noun to one syllable.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个借来的名词缩成一个音节。

items.meaning: a journey, an expedition, a troop
items.example: The noun supplies the going that the compound needs.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词所需的「出行」义。

items.meaning: to travel; a journey; the price of travel
items.example: The modern noun keeps the journey and adds the cost.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词保留「行程」，又添上「花费」。

items.example: Welfare and warfare both end in this element, though only one begins with war.
items.exampleCN: welfare 与 warfare 都以这个成分结尾，尽管只有一个以 war 开头。

items.example: The compound names the going out to fight, not the price of a ticket.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名的是出征作战，而不是票价。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun of strife into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「争斗」名词变成一个人。

items.meaningCN: 具有战争性质的；好战的
items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of manner out of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词造出表示性质的形容词。

definition_zh: （criterion 的复数）标准；准则；尺度
definition_en: plural of criterion: the standards by which something is judged or decided
core_image: 一把用来筛人的筛子，孔的大小就是标准
scene: 面试桌上堆着简历，筛选表列着三条硬性条件。 The HR officer wrote three hard criteria into the screening form.
sceneCN: 这里 criteria 是「标准、准则」（第 1 个义项：判断事物的依据，复数）；句意：人力资源专员把三条硬性标准写进了筛选表。

pos.zh: （criterion 的复数）标准；准则；尺度

senses.title: Standards used for judging
senses.definition: the standards or rules by which something is judged, compared, or decided
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断、比较或决定某事物的标准或规则
senses.example: The judges scored the entries against five criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 评委按五条标准给参赛作品打分。
senses.why: Greek kritērion meant 'means for judging', from krinein 'to separate, decide'. Criteria are the tools that separate the good from the bad, the eligible from the not.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kritērion 意为“判断的工具”，来自 krinein“分开、决定”。criteria 就是把人或事物分成好坏、合格与不合格的工具。

senses.title: Singular and plural: criterion, criteria
senses.titleCN: 单数与复数：criterion 与 criteria
senses.definition: criteria is the plural of criterion; 'a criteria' is nonstandard because criteria already means more than one
senses.definitionCN: criteria 是 criterion 的复数；“a criteria”不合标准，因为 criteria 本身已表示多个
senses.example: One criterion, two criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 一个标准是 criterion，两个标准是 criteria。
senses.why: criterion is a Greek neuter noun in -on, and Greek neuters of this type take -a in the plural. The plural therefore has no -s: kriterion becomes kritēria.
senses.whyCN: criterion 是希腊语中以 -on 结尾的中性名词，这类希腊中性名词的复数用 -a。因此复数不加 -s：kriterion 变成 kritēria。

senses.title: Selection and admission criteria
senses.definition: the published standards used to choose among applicants
senses.definitionCN: 用于在申请者中挑选的公开标准
senses.example: The scholarship has clear selection criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金有明确的选拔标准。
senses.why: An institution applies the sieve publicly so that the decision can be defended. Criteria make a choice look less arbitrary.
senses.whyCN: 机构公开使用这把筛子，使决定可以被辩护。标准让选择看起来不那么任意。

senses.title: Diagnostic criteria in medicine
senses.definition: the agreed set of symptoms and tests that must be present before a diagnosis is made
senses.definitionCN: 作出诊断前必须出现的、经同行约定的症状与检查指标
senses.example: The diagnosis follows international criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断遵循国际标准。
senses.why: Medicine separates symptoms into categories that decide a case. The Greek root's 'separate and decide' is here a clinical procedure.
senses.whyCN: 医学把症状分进不同类别，以此决定病例。希腊词根的“分开并判定”在这里是一项临床程序。

senses.title: Design and quality criteria
senses.definition: the measurable requirements a product or structure must meet
senses.definitionCN: 产品或结构必须满足的可测量要求
senses.example: The bridge was tested against safety criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按安全标准进行了测试。
senses.why: Engineering turns judgement into numbers so that pass or fail can be checked. The criteria are the ruler laid against the object.
senses.whyCN: 工程把判断变成数字，使合格与否可以被检查。标准就是贴在对象上的那把尺。

senses.title: Eligibility criteria
senses.definition: the conditions a person must satisfy to qualify for a benefit, programme, or right
senses.definitionCN: 个人为获得福利、项目或权利必须满足的条件
senses.example: Applicants must meet the eligibility criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须符合资格标准。
senses.why: This is the legal sieve: it separates those entitled from those not. The decision is made before any individual case is heard.
senses.whyCN: 这是法律筛子：它把有资格的人和无资格的人分开。决定在个案被听取之前就已由标准作出。

senses.title: Acceptance criteria in projects
senses.definition: the predefined conditions that must be met before work is accepted as complete
senses.definitionCN: 工作被接受为完成之前必须满足的预定条件
senses.example: A task is done when its acceptance criteria are met.
senses.exampleCN: 当验收标准满足时，任务才算完成。
senses.why: Project management fixes the standards before the work starts. The criteria decide when the deliverable is accepted, so 'done' becomes a judgement with a rule.
senses.whyCN: 项目管理在开工前先固定标准。标准决定交付物何时被接受，于是“完成”变成一个有规则的判断。

senses.title: Research and measurement criteria
senses.definition: the rules used to decide which data or methods count as valid in a study
senses.definitionCN: 用于判定哪些数据或方法在研究中等效的规则
senses.example: The study defined criteria for valid samples.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究为有效样本设定了标准。
senses.why: Research separates usable evidence from noise. Criteria are the stated conditions under which a sample or result is admitted.
senses.whyCN: 研究把可用证据与噪声分开。标准就是宣布样本或结果被接纳时所依据的条件。

senses.title: Greek -on/-a plurals
senses.definition: the morphological pattern in which Greek neuter nouns ending in -on form their plural in -a
senses.definitionCN: 以 -on 结尾的希腊中性名词用 -a 构成复数的词形模式
senses.example: Criterion/criteria follows the Greek pattern, like phenomenon/phenomena.
senses.exampleCN: criterion/criteria 遵循希腊语模式，就像 phenomenon/phenomena。
senses.why: The -a ending is not an English plural but a Greek one carried over. Once you see the pattern, criteria, phenomena and automata stop looking irregular.
senses.whyCN: -a 词尾不是英语复数，而是被保留下来的希腊语复数。看懂这个模式后，criteria、phenomena、automata 就不再显得不规则。

intro.en: Criteria is not an English plural made with -s; it is the Greek plural of criterion. The singular ends in -on, the plural in -a, and both come from krinein 'to separate, decide'.
intro.cn: criteria 不是用 -s 构成的英语复数，而是 criterion 的希腊语复数。单数结尾 -on，复数结尾 -a，两者都来自 krinein“分开、判定”。

items.en: criterion is first recorded in English meaning 'a standard for judging'. The Greek plural criteria came with it.
items.cn: criterion 于 17 世纪 20 年代最早进入英语，意为“判断的标准”；希腊语复数 criteria 随之进入。

items.en: From Greek kritērion 'means for judging, standard', from kritēs 'judge', from krinein 'to separate, decide'.
items.cn: 来自希腊语 kritērion“判断的工具、标准”，出自 kritēs“法官”，再上溯 krinein“分开、判定”。

items.en: kriterion is a neuter noun in -on; Greek neuters of this class form the plural in -a. Hence kriterion → kritēria, with no -s.
items.cn: kriterion 是以 -on 结尾的中性名词；这类希腊中性名词复数用 -a。因此 kriterion → kritēria，不加 -s。

items.en: krinein is traced to PIE *krei- 'to sieve, discriminate, distinguish', also behind crisis and critic. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: krinein 被追溯到原始印欧语 *krei-“筛、区分、辨别”，crisis 和 critic 也出自这里。该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: English uses criteria as the plural; in the 20c. 'a criteria' spreads in informal writing even though the singular is criterion.
items.cn: 英语用 criteria 作复数；20 世纪“a criteria”在非正式写作中扩散，尽管单数形式是 criterion。

items.en: Modern technical usage fixes phrases such as diagnostic criteria, selection criteria and acceptance criteria, where the plural is almost always required.
items.cn: 现代技术用法固定了 diagnostic criteria、selection criteria、acceptance criteria 等短语，这些短语几乎总用复数。

note.en: The first group shares krinein 'separate, decide'; the second group separates standards, benchmarks, measuring tools and plain rules.
note.cn: 第一组共享 krinein“分开、判定”；第二组区分标准、基准、测量工具和普通规则。

entries.definition: one standard for judging. It is the singular that criteria replaces in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 一条判断标准。它就是 criteria 在复数中替换掉的单数形式。

entries.definition: decisive, or involving judgement and criticism. It shares krinein 'decide'.
entries.definitionCN: 关键的，或涉及判断与批评的。它共享 krinein“判定”。

entries.definition: a turning point that demands a decision. Greek krisis meant 'a separating, a decision'.
entries.definitionCN: 需要作出决定的转折点。希腊语 krisis 意为“分离、判定”。

entries.definition: a level of quality or a rule used for comparison. It is broader and can be singular or plural.
entries.definitionCN: 用于比较的质量水平或规则。它更宽泛，可单数也可复数。

entries.definition: a known reference point against which performance is measured. It is usually one point, not a set.
entries.definitionCN: 用来衡量表现的已知参照点。它通常是一个点，不是一套。

entries.definition: an instrument or a standard for measuring. It stresses measurement more than judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 测量仪器或衡量标准。它更强调测量，而不是判断。

entries.definition: a standard used to compare quality or success. It is informal and often singular.
entries.definitionCN: 用来比较质量或成功的标准。它偏口语，常作单数。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Greek krinein 'separate, decide' gives criterion, criteria, critic, critical and crisis. The -on/-a plural is a Greek pattern, not an English one.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：希腊语 krinein“分开、判定”给出 criterion、criteria、critic、critical、crisis。-on/-a 复数是希腊语模式，不是英语模式。

normal.en: One criterion, two criteria. If you remember the Greek -on/-a pair, you will never write 'a criteria'.
normal.cn: 一个 criterion，两个 criteria。记住希腊语 -on/-a 这一对，就不会写出 a criteria。

normal.en: Criterion, critic, critical and crisis all contain krinein 'separate, decide'. A criterion is the tool that separates.
normal.cn: criterion、critic、critical、crisis 都含 krinein“分开、判定”。criterion 就是那把用来分开的工具。

normal.en: Selection criteria are the sieve holes: change the holes, and a different group passes through.
normal.cn: 选拔标准就是筛子的孔：换掉孔径，通过的群体就变了。

normal.en: Diagnostic criteria decide a case before treatment begins, just as a judge decides before sentence.
normal.cn: 诊断标准在治疗开始前就决定了病例，就像法官在量刑前先判定。

normal.en: Acceptance criteria are written before the work starts, so 'done' is defined in advance.
normal.cn: 验收标准在开工前就写好，所以“完成”是被预先定义的。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve held over a pile of applicants. The holes are the criteria; the sieve does not argue with anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一把筛子悬在一堆申请者上方。孔就是标准；筛子不跟任何人争论。

abstract.en: A criterion is a ruler laid against a thing. Remove the ruler, and 'better' and 'worse' become opinions again.
abstract.cn: criterion 是贴在某物上的一把尺。拿掉尺子，“更好”和“更差”就又变回意见。

abstract.en: The Greek plural -a is a fossil: the word still carries the shape of the language that made it.
abstract.cn: 希腊语复数 -a 是一块化石：这个词仍带着制造它的那种语言的形状。

examples.en: The panel listed the criteria before reading any application.
examples.cn: 评审组在阅读任何申请之前先列出了标准。

examples.en: No single criterion can capture teaching quality.
examples.cn: 没有任何单一标准能完全衡量教学质量。

examples.en: The new criteria take effect next semester.
examples.cn: 新标准下学期生效。

dict_mnemonic.text: “克瑞特里亚”——克瑞特里亚拿尺子把候选人分成合格与不合格 → criteria 标准（criterion 的复数）

root: 希腊语 kritērion“判断的依据”，来自 krinein“分开、判定”，核心是“用来筛分好坏的那把尺”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of criteria, all one act of judging: standards in general, the plural rule, selection, diagnosis, design, eligibility, acceptance, research, and the Greek -on/-a pattern that explains the form.
sensesIntro.cn: criteria 的九个义项都是同一个“判定”：一般标准、复数规则、选拔、诊断、设计、资格、验收、研究，以及解释其词形的希腊语 -on/-a 模式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve whose holes decide what passes through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把筛子，孔的大小决定谁能通过。

branches.en: FORM: the plural means more than one standard, and the Greek -a ending explains why.
branches.cn: 形式：复数表示不止一条标准，希腊语 -a 词尾解释了这个形式。

branches.en: ADMISSION: selection and eligibility criteria decide who is let in.
branches.cn: 准入：选拔与资格标准决定谁被放进来。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: diagnosis and research criteria decide what counts as a valid case.
branches.cn: 证据：诊断与研究标准决定什么算有效案例。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: design and acceptance criteria decide whether work passes.
branches.cn: 生产：设计与验收标准决定工作是否通过。

branches.en: MORPHOLOGY: the Greek neuter pattern keeps the plural separate from English -s.
branches.cn: 词形：希腊中性名词模式使这个复数不走英语 -s。

intro.en: criteria has no live English affixes. Its ending is a Greek plural, and its relatives are separate borrowings from the same krinein family.
intro.cn: criteria 没有活的英语词缀。它的词尾是希腊语复数，同族词是从同一个 krinein 词族分别借入的。

latinIntro.en: The family comes from Greek, not Latin: krinein 'separate, decide' gives critic, critical, criticism, crisis and criterion.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族来自希腊语而非拉丁语：krinein“分开、判定”给出 critic、critical、criticism、crisis、criterion。

items.meaningCN: 单数形式：一条判断标准
items.example: Cost is only one criterion among several.
items.exampleCN: 成本只是若干标准中的一条。

items.meaning: decisive, or involving judgement and analysis
items.meaningCN: 关键的；批判性的（能够判断）
items.example: Critical thinking compares evidence before deciding.
items.exampleCN: 批判性思维在决定前先比较证据。

items.meaning: a person who judges and comments on works
items.meaningCN: 批评家；评论者（作出判断的人）
items.example: The critic praised the film's restraint.
items.exampleCN: 评论者称赞了影片的克制。

items.meaning: a turning point that demands a decision
items.meaningCN: 危机；转折点（必须作出决定的时刻）
items.example: The shortage became a crisis by midwinter.
items.exampleCN: 短缺在隆冬时演变成危机。

items.meaning: the work of judging faults, or a considered judgment
items.meaningCN: 批评；评论（-ism 表示活动或论说）
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章招来尖锐的批评。

items.meaning: to judge or point out faults
items.meaningCN: 批评；评判（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: a detailed judgment of a work
items.meaningCN: 评论；评析（源自希腊语 kritikē“评判术”）
items.example: She wrote a critique of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一篇对该计划的评析。

items.meaning: in a judging way, or crucially
items.meaningCN: 批判性地；关键地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 他批判性地读了这份草稿。

latinEntries.meaning: to judge and point out faults
latinEntries.meaningCN: 批评；指出缺点（作出判断）

latinEntries.meaning: a detailed judgement of a work
latinEntries.meaningCN: 评论；批评文章（对作品的详细判断）

latinEntries.meaning: pretending to have beliefs one does not hold
latinEntries.meaningCN: 虚伪（希腊语“演戏、扮演”，与 krinein 同一语源群）

definition_zh: 正当理由；辩护；辩解；（神学）称义；（排版）两端对齐
definition_en: the act of showing that something is right or reasonable; a reason given in defence; (theology) the state of being made righteous; (printing) the alignment of text to both margins
core_image: 天平两端分别放上指控与证据，指针最终停在水平位置
scene: 听证会上，发言人出示三份检测报告。 The three reports are the justification for that decision.
sceneCN: 这里 justification 是「正当理由」（第 1 个义项：证明某决定合理的依据）；句意：这三份报告就是该决定的正当理由。

pos.zh: 正当理由；辩护（可数指一条理由，不可数指证明合理的过程）
（神学）称义；（排版）两端对齐（专业义，常带修饰语）

collocations.zh: 对 A 的正当理由

derivatives.zh: 有正当理由的；可辩护的

senses.title: Showing something to be reasonable
senses.definition: the act of demonstrating that a decision, claim, or action is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 证明某个决定、主张或行为正确或合理的行为
senses.example: The report offers a strong justification for raising the minimum wage.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为提高最低工资提供了有力理由。
senses.why: Justification is justify + -ation. Justify comes from Late Latin justificare, justus 'just' + facere 'to make': to make something just, or to show that it already is. The suffix names the act of making that showing.
senses.whyCN: justification 是 justify + -ation。justify 源自晚期拉丁语 justificare，即 justus“公正”+ facere“使”：使某事成为公正的，或表明它本就公正。后缀命名的是这一“表明”的行为。

senses.title: A defence offered for conduct
senses.definition: a reason put forward to defend an action that others may criticise
senses.definitionCN: 为他人可能批评的行为提出的辩护理由
senses.example: His justification for leaving early was that the trains had stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 他早退的理由是列车已经停运。
senses.why: This sense is personal and often defensive: the justification is offered after the act, to answer a challenge. The word assumes a critic exists, which is why it often sounds like an argument rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是个人化的，常带防御性：理由在行为之后提出，用来回应质疑。这个词预设有一个批评者存在，所以它常听起来像论辩而非证明。

senses.title: Justification in theology
senses.definition: the act by which God is said to make a sinner righteous, central to Reformation disputes
senses.definitionCN: 上帝使罪人成为义人的行为，是宗教改革争论的核心
senses.example: Luther taught justification by faith alone.
senses.exampleCN: 路德教导“唯独因信称义”。
senses.why: Theology uses the word in its strongest sense: not a claim that someone is just, but a change that makes them so. The Latin facere 'make' is doing real work here, unlike in the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 神学用这个词的最强意义：不是声称某人公正，而是使其成为公正的改变。这里拉丁语 facere“使”真正起作用，与日常义不同。

senses.title: Legal or official grounds
senses.definition: the legal grounds that make an action permissible or a claim admissible
senses.definitionCN: 使某行为被允许或某主张可被接受的法律依据
senses.example: The court found no legal justification for the search.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这次搜查没有法律依据。
senses.why: Law asks not whether an action was reasonable in general but whether it was authorised. Justification here is a formal finding that the required grounds existed.
senses.whyCN: 法律不问行为在一般意义上是否合理，而问它是否被授权。这里的 justification 是对“所需依据确实存在”的正式认定。

senses.title: Text alignment in printing
senses.definition: the adjustment of spacing so that lines of text align evenly at the margin
senses.definitionCN: 调整字距，使各行文字在页边对齐
senses.example: Full justification stretched the words across the narrow column.
senses.exampleCN: 两端对齐把字距拉宽以填满窄栏。
senses.why: This sense comes from the same Latin root by a different path: to justify a line is to make its edges 'just' or exact. The printing trade borrowed the moral word and gave it a mechanical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自同一拉丁词根但路径不同：让一行文字的边缘“正”或精确。印刷业借用了这个道德词，赋予它机械含义。

senses.title: Epistemic justification
senses.definition: the reason or warrant that makes a belief reasonable to hold
senses.definitionCN: 使某个信念有理由被持有的依据或保证
senses.example: Philosophers distinguish justification from mere belief.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家把证成与单纯的相信区分开来。
senses.why: Philosophy asks what makes a belief acceptable rather than merely held. Justification here is the warrant, and the debates are about whether it must be internal, external, or both.
senses.whyCN: 哲学追问是什么使一个信念可被接受，而不只是被持有。这里的 justification 是保证，争论在于它必须是内在的、外在的，还是两者兼有。

senses.title: Grounds in an argument
senses.definition: the premises or evidence that support a conclusion in reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 推理中支持结论的前提或证据
senses.example: The justification for the inference lies in the correlation itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这一推断的依据就在相关性本身。
senses.why: Logic needs a word for the support relation between premises and conclusion. Justification names that relation, not the psychological confidence of the person reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要一个词来指前提与结论之间的支持关系。justification 命名这一关系，而不是推理者的心理确信。

senses.title: Business case for a request
senses.definition: a written case showing why a purchase, project, or budget is worth approving
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项采购、项目或预算值得批准的书面论证
senses.example: The manager attached a two-page justification to the purchase order.
senses.exampleCN: 经理在采购单后附了两页理由说明。
senses.why: Organizations require justification to make decisions auditable: someone must show that the cost buys a benefit. The word turns a preference into a record.
senses.whyCN: 组织要求理由说明，是为了让决策可被审计：必须有人证明这笔成本换来了收益。这个词把偏好变成记录。

intro.en: Justification is justify + -ation. Justify comes from Late Latin justificare, from justus 'just, lawful' and facere 'to make'. Justus itself goes back to ius 'law, right', the same root that gives justice, judge, and jury.
intro.cn: justification 是 justify + -ation。justify 源自晚期拉丁语 justificare，由 justus“公正、合法”与 facere“使”构成。justus 本身上溯 ius“法、权利”，同一词根还给出 justice、judge 与 jury。

items.en: Latin ius (genitive iuris) meant 'law, right, justice'. Justus 'lawful, just' came from it, and iudex 'judge' was literally ius + dicere 'say the law'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ius（属格 iuris）意为“法、权利、正义”。justus“合法的、公正的”由此而来，而 iudex“法官”字面是 ius + dicere“说出法律”。

items.en: Justificare combined justus with facere 'to make': to make someone or something just, or to show it as just. The noun justificatio named this making.
items.cn: justificare 把 justus 与 facere“使”结合：使某人或某物成为公正的，或表明其为公正。名词 justificatio 命名这一“使之”过程。

items.en: English justification entered through Old French in the fourteenth century. The word carried both the everyday sense 'defence' and the theological sense 'being made righteous'.
items.cn: 英语 justification 于 14 世纪经古法语进入。这个词同时带有日常义“辩护”与神学义“被称为义”。

items.en: The Reformation made justification a contested technical term: whether it is a change in the sinner or a verdict about them. The word's later legal and philosophical uses inherited this precision.
items.cn: 宗教改革使 justification 成为有争议的术语：它是罪人身上的改变，还是关于他的判决。这个词后来的法律与哲学用法继承了这种精确性。

items.en: The printing trade used 'justify' for making a line's edges exact, which produced the noun 'justification' in typography. The moral word acquired a mechanical sense.
items.cn: 印刷业用 justify 指把一行文字的边缘弄“正”，由此产生排版义 justification。这个道德词获得机械含义。

items.en: Analytic philosophy made justification a central term for the warrant of belief, while organizations made 'justification' a written business case. The word now covers proof, defence, and record.
items.cn: 分析哲学使 justification 成为信念保证的核心术语，组织则把 justification 变成书面商业论证。这个词如今覆盖证明、辩护与记录。

note.en: The look-alike group separates words built on ius 'law' or on other roots; the near-meaning group separates reason, defence, and excuse.
note.cn: 形近组区分建立在 ius“法”或其他词根上的词；近义组区分“理由”“辩护”与“借口”。

entries.tag: same ius root noun of rightness
entries.definition: fairness or the administration of law. It comes from Latin iustitia, from iustus, but names the virtue itself rather than the argument for a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 公平或司法。它来自拉丁语 iustitia，源自 iustus，但命名的是美德本身，而不是为某个决定作论证。

entries.definition: a decision or opinion. It comes from iudicium, built on ius + dicere 'say', so it names the verdict, not the grounds offered for it.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判断。它来自 iudicium，由 ius + dicere“说”构成，因此命名的是判决，而非为其提出的依据。

entries.definition: the checking of a fact or claim. It comes from verus 'true', and asks whether something is factually correct rather than whether it is justified.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实或主张的核查。它来自 verus“真”，问的是某事在事实上是否正确，而不是它是否有正当理由。

entries.definition: a cause or explanation for something. It can be neutral or trivial, while justification implies that the reason is adequate to defend the act.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的原因或解释。它可以是中性或琐碎的，而 justification 暗示该理由足以为此行为辩护。

entries.definition: an argument or action that protects against criticism. Justification is the content of such a defence: the grounds that make it work.
entries.definitionCN: 为抵御批评而提出的论证或行动。justification 是这种辩护的内容：使它成立的那些依据。

entries.definition: a reason offered to avoid blame, often not accepted by the hearer. It is weaker than justification, which claims genuine adequacy.
entries.definitionCN: 为逃避责备而给的理由，常不被听者接受。它比 justification 弱，后者声称确实充分。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: ius 'law' + facere 'make', the theological phrase justification by faith, and the typographic use of justified text.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：ius“法”+ facere“使”、神学说法 justification by faith，以及排版中的 justified text。

normal.en: justus means 'lawful' and facere means 'make': justification is making a case stand as right.
normal.cn: justus 意为“合法的”，facere 意为“使”：justification 就是让一个说法站得住、显得正当。

normal.en: justice, judge, jury, and justification all descend from ius, the Latin word for law.
normal.cn: justice、judge、jury、justification 都源自 ius，即拉丁语“法”。

normal.en: In theology the word is strongest: it makes a person righteous, not merely calls them so.
normal.cn: 在神学里这个词最强：它使人成为义人，而不只是称他为义人。

normal.en: In printing, to justify a line is to make its edges exact — 'just' in the geometric sense.
normal.cn: 在印刷中，justify a line 是把行边弄“正”——几何意义上的“正”。

normal.en: A purchase order needs a justification so that the spending can be audited later.
normal.cn: 采购单需要理由说明，好让这笔支出日后可被审计。

abstract.en: The word always answers a challenge: it exists because someone might say 'no' or 'why'.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是在回应质疑：它之所以存在，是因为有人可能说“不行”或“为什么”。

abstract.en: It claims adequacy, not truth — a justification can be sound and the decision still wrong.
abstract.cn: 它主张的是充分性，而不是真理性——理由可以成立，决定仍然可能是错的。

abstract.en: From courtroom to column width, the same idea recurs: making edges come out even.
abstract.cn: 从法庭到栏宽，同一个想法反复出现：让边缘变得齐整。

examples.en: There is no justification for treating one group differently.
examples.cn: 没有正当理由区别对待某个群体。

examples.en: The theologian wrote about justification by faith alone.
examples.cn: 这位神学家论述了“唯独因信称义”。

examples.en: The columns look tidy because the text is fully justified.
examples.cn: 因为文字采用了两端对齐，各栏看起来很整齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扎斯提飞开心”——把理由“扎”实、“提”出来，让人飞着也开心地接受 → justification 正当理由、辩护

root: 拉丁语 ius/iur-“法、权利”→ iustus“公正的”+ facere“使”+ -ation；字面义“使之公正、使之站得住”，核心是“为某决定提供充分依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of justification all answer the question 'why is this acceptable?': a decision, a conduct, a sinner, a search, a line of type, a belief, an inference, and a purchase. The word always offers grounds, and grounds can always be challenged.
sensesIntro.cn: justification 的八个义项都在回答“这为什么可以被接受？”：一个决定、一种行为、一个罪人、一次搜查、一行文字、一个信念、一次推断、一笔采购。这个词总是提供依据，而依据总是可以被质疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with accusation on one side and evidence on the other, settling level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端放指控、一端放证据，最终停在水平。

branches.en: EVERYDAY DEFENCE: a decision or an action is shown to be reasonable, often after criticism.
branches.cn: 日常辩护：决定或行为被表明合理，常在批评之后。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: theology and law decide whether the grounds actually transform or authorise.
branches.cn: 权威：神学与法律判定依据究竟能改变人，还是能授权行为。

branches.en: TYPOGRAPHY: the same word makes a line's edges exact.
branches.cn: 排版：同一个词让一行文字的边缘变得精确。

branches.en: REASONING: philosophy and logic ask what warrants a belief or an inference.
branches.cn: 推理：哲学与逻辑追问是什么为信念或推断提供保证。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: a written case turns a preference into an auditable record.
branches.cn: 管理：书面论证把偏好变成可审计的记录。

intro.en: Justification is justify + -ation, from Late Latin justificare (justus + facere). The family is divided between derivatives of justify and the ius 'law' relatives justice, just, judge, and jury.
intro.cn: justification 是 justify + -ation，源自晚期拉丁语 justificare（justus + facere）。家族分为 justify 的派生词与 ius“法”的亲属词 justice、just、judge、jury。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius (genitive iuris) 'law, right' produced iustus 'just', iustitia 'justice', iudex 'judge' (ius + dicere 'say'), and iudicium 'judgement'. Justificare is a Late Latin compound of iustus with facere 'make'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius（属格 iuris）“法、权利”产生 iustus“公正的”、iustitia“正义”、iudex“法官”（ius + dicere“说”）、iudicium“判断”。justificare 是晚期拉丁语中 iustus 与 facere“使”的复合词。

items.meaning: grounds that show something is right; alignment
items.meaningCN: 正当理由；辩护；对齐（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: No justification was given for the delay.
items.exampleCN: 对这次延误没有给出理由。

items.meaning: to show to be right; to align text
items.meaningCN: 证明正当；为……辩护；对齐（源自晚期拉丁语）
items.example: How can you justify the expense?
items.exampleCN: 你如何证明这笔开支合理？

items.meaning: able to be defended as right
items.meaningCN: 有正当理由的（-able 表可能）
items.example: The delay was justifiable in the circumstances.
items.exampleCN: 在当时情况下，延误是有理由的。

items.meaningCN: 有理由地（-ly 构成副词）
没有正当理由的（un- 表否定）
辩护性的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 他加了一条辩解性脚注。

items.structure: Latin iudex, from ius + dicere 'say the law'

definition_zh: 轴；轴线；中心线；联盟轴心
definition_en: an imaginary line about which a body turns; a central line or alliance
core_image: 陀螺上那根看不见的线：整团旋转都围着它
scene: 地理课上老师转动地球仪，指尖点着南北极的连线。 The earth spins on its axis once a day.
sceneCN: 这里 axis 指「自转轴」（第 1 个义项：旋转所围绕的线）；句意：地球每天绕轴自转一周。

pos.zh: 轴；轴线
轴心；中心联盟

derivatives.zh: 公理（拼写相关但词源不同，仅形近提示）

senses.title: The line a spinning body turns about
senses.definition: an imaginary straight line around which a rotating body turns
senses.definitionCN: 旋转体绕之转动的假想直线
senses.example: The planet tilts on its axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗行星的自转轴是倾斜的。
senses.why: Latin axis named the axle of a wheel; every wheel implies its invisible line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 axis 本指车轮的轴；有轮必有那条无形的线。

senses.title: A reference line in graphs
senses.definition: a fixed reference line for measuring coordinates on a graph
senses.definitionCN: 坐标图上作度量基准的固定直线
senses.example: Plot cost on the vertical axis.
senses.exampleCN: 把成本标在纵轴上。
senses.why: A graph freezes rotation into a measuring line: the axle becomes a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 坐标图把旋转抽象成度量线：轮轴化为标尺。

senses.title: A central line of a body or structure
senses.definition: a real or imaginary central line of symmetry in a body, building, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 身体、建筑或规划中真实或假想的中心对称线
senses.example: The garden is laid out along a central axis.
senses.exampleCN: 花园沿中轴线布局。
senses.why: What everything is arranged around is still the axle idea, made architectural.
senses.whyCN: 万物环绕之线仍是轮轴意象的建筑化。

senses.title: An alliance between powers
senses.definition: a political alliance around which other powers group, as the Axis powers
senses.definitionCN: 以某方为核心的联盟，如轴心国
senses.example: The Axis powers were defeated in 1945.
senses.exampleCN: 轴心国于 1945 年战败。
senses.why: Mussolini spoke of an axis between Rome and Berlin: a line other states were to revolve around.
senses.whyCN: 墨索里尼称罗马与柏林之间有条「轴」，他国应绕之旋转。

senses.title: The second cervical vertebra
senses.definition: the second cervical vertebra on which the head rotates
senses.definitionCN: 头部赖以转动的第二颈椎
senses.example: The axis allows the head to turn side to side.
senses.exampleCN: 枢椎使头部得以左右转动。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the wheel word for the vertebra the head pivots on.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借轮轴之词命名头部转动的椎骨。

senses.title: A deer of the spotted kind
senses.definition: a small Asian deer with a spotted coat, the axis deer
senses.definitionCN: 产于亚洲的梅花点小鹿，称 axis deer
senses.example: Axis deer graze at the forest edge.
senses.exampleCN: 轴鹿在林缘吃草。
senses.why: The deer's name is a separate Latin word axis, a spotted Hindoo deer of old texts.
senses.whyCN: 此鹿名为拉丁语另一词 axis，古籍中的点斑鹿，与「轴」无关。

senses.title: In crystallography and optics
senses.definition: a principal direction in a crystal along which light or structure is measured
senses.definitionCN: 晶体中测量光性或结构的主方向
senses.example: Quartz has three axes of symmetry.
senses.exampleCN: 石英有三条对称轴。
senses.why: Science extends the reference-line sense to any principal direction of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 科学把基准线义扩展到一切主测量方向。

senses.title: Plural axes in mathematics
senses.definition: the plural form used of several such lines
senses.definitionCN: 指多条此类直线的复数形式
senses.example: The diagram shows all three axes.
senses.exampleCN: 图中三条轴线全部画出。
senses.why: The plural keeps the Greek-style ending, like crisis to crises.
senses.whyCN: 复数保留希腊式词尾，如 crisis 变 crises。

intro.en: Latin axis, axle, goes back to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning to drive or urge, the same source as Greek axon and English axle.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 axis「轮轴」可溯至原始印欧语词根「驱赶、推动」，与希腊语 axon、英语 axle 同源。

items.en: The root ag- meant to drive, to move a thing by force.
items.cn: 词根 ag- 意为驱赶、用力移动。

items.en: A derivative aks- named the rod that drives a wheel: the axle.
items.cn: 派生 aks- 指驱动轮子的杆：车轴。

items.en: Latin axis meant the axle of a wheel or the North Pole axis of the heavens.
items.cn: 拉丁语 axis 指轮轴，亦指天球旋转的极轴。

items.en: Greek axon, axle, is the same word, and survives in biology.
items.cn: 希腊语 axon 同源，存于生物学「轴突」。

items.en: English took axis from Latin for the axle and soon for the celestial line.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入 axis，先指轮轴，继而指天轴。

items.en: The graph, anatomy, and political senses grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 坐标轴、解剖与政治义成于十九、二十世纪。

note.en: Group one holds the axle family and look-alikes; group two holds the central-line field.
note.cn: 第一组收轮轴词族与形近词；第二组收「中心线」义场。

entries.definition: the rod a wheel turns on; the everyday cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 轮轴；axis 的日常同源词。

entries.definition: a nerve fiber; the Greek form of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 神经轴突；同一词的希腊形式。

entries.definition: a chopping tool; older spelling ax, no kin to axis.
entries.definitionCN: 斧子；与 axis 词源无关，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: the point on which something turns.
entries.definitionCN: 旋转的中心点。

entries.definition: the central part of a wheel; a center of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 轮毂；活动中心。

entries.definition: the outer edge, as against the central axis.
entries.definitionCN: 外围、边缘；与中轴相对。

normalIntro.en: axis is the Latin axle: everything that turns, turns around it.
normalIntro.cn: axis 即拉丁语轮轴：一切旋转都绕它进行。

normal.en: Root: Latin axis, axle.
normal.cn: 词根：拉丁语 axis「轮轴」。

normal.en: Kin: axle and axon are the same word.
normal.cn: 同源：axle 与 axon 同出一词。

normal.en: Plural: axes, like crisis to crises.
normal.cn: 复数 axes，如 crisis 变 crises。

normal.en: Adjective: axial, as in axial tilt.
normal.cn: 形容词 axial，如 axial tilt「轴倾角」。

normal.en: Politics: the Rome–Berlin axis of the 1930s.
normal.cn: 政治：1930 年代的罗马—柏林轴心。

abstract.en: See the invisible line through the spinning top.
abstract.cn: 看陀螺中那根无形的线。

abstract.en: Axis is the still point the whirl pretends to own.
abstract.cn: axis 是旋转假装拥有的那个不动之点。

abstract.en: Picture planets strung on a silver rod.
abstract.cn: 想象行星串在一根银杆上。

examples.en: The gyroscope keeps steady as long as its axis stays fixed.
examples.cn: 只要轴向不变，陀螺仪就能保持稳定。

examples.en: Label the horizontal axis with the months of the year.
examples.cn: 给横轴标上月份。

examples.en: The two nations formed an axis against their neighbors.
examples.cn: 两国结成轴心以对抗邻国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克西斯」——爱围着一条克（刻）好的线转，这条线就是轴

root: 出自拉丁语 axis「轮轴、极轴」，溯至原始印欧语词根 *ag-「驱动」的派生形式 *aks-；与希腊语 axon「轴突」、英语 axle「轮轴」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run one line through wheel, graph, city plan, alliance, vertebra, deer, crystal, and the plural form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项贯穿一条线：车轮、坐标、城市布局、联盟、颈椎、鹿、晶体与复数形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the still line everything turns around.
core.cn: 核心意象：万物绕之旋转的那条不动的线。

branches.en: Wheel and vertebra share the pivot of motion.
branches.cn: 车轮与颈椎同享「转动枢点」。

branches.en: Graph and crystal use the line to measure.
branches.cn: 坐标与晶体都借这条线来度量。

branches.en: The city plan turns the line into symmetry.
branches.cn: 城市规划把这条线化作对称。

branches.en: Politics imagines states revolving on a line.
branches.cn: 政治想象各国绕一条线旋转。

branches.en: A second Latin word and the plural close the entry.
branches.cn: 另一拉丁词与复数形式收尾。

intro.en: The axis family is small and old: a single Indo-European root gives the Latin, Greek, and English axle words.
intro.cn: axis 词族小而古老：一个印欧词根生出拉丁、希腊与英语的轮轴词。

latinIntro.en: Latin kin are direct: axis itself and its derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词直接：axis 本词及其派生。

items.meaning: rod on which a wheel turns

latinEntries.meaning: axle of a wheel; polar line of the heavens

latinEntries.meaningCN: 腋；后成 axillary（仅形近，词源不同支）

definition_zh: adj. （言辞）夸夸其谈的，浮夸空洞的
definition_en: of speech or writing, pompous and inflated, with grand words but little meaning
core_image: 讲台上的人声音越来越大，词句越来越空，句尾却没有落点
scene: 那场演讲满是宏大的词，散场后没人记得一句。 The speech was bombastic, full of grand words that nobody could afterwards recall.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bombastic 形容言辞浮夸空洞；句意是那场演讲满是大词，散场后无人记得。

pos.zh: 夸夸其谈的；浮夸的

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Pompous and inflated in speech
senses.definition: using high-sounding words that sound impressive but carry little substance
senses.definitionCN: 使用听来堂皇却少有实质的夸张词语
senses.example: The minister answered a simple question in bombastic terms.
senses.exampleCN: 部长用一个简单的问题，答出一串浮夸的辞令。
senses.why: Bombast was the cotton used to pad a garment, and padded speech is speech stuffed with air.
senses.whyCN: bombast 原指给衣服填塞的棉絮，而「填充的言辞」就是塞满空气的话。

senses.title: Overloaded in style
senses.definition: of writing, heavily ornamented and overblown rather than clear
senses.definitionCN: 文章装饰过重、夸张而缺乏清晰
senses.example: The essay is bombastic where it should be plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在该朴素的地方反而堆砌。
senses.why: The padding metaphor moves from a stuffed coat to a sentence stuffed with ornament.
senses.whyCN: 「填塞」的比喻从塞满棉衣转到塞满装饰的句子。

intro.en: Bombastic comes from bombast, the cotton used to pad clothes, from Old French bombace and Latin bombax.
intro.cn: bombastic 来自 bombast（填衣用的棉絮），经古法语 bombace 上溯拉丁语 bombax。

items.en: Bombax is cotton or cotton wool.
items.cn: bombax 意为棉花、棉絮。

items.en: Bombace names the padding in a garment.
items.cn: bombace 指衣物的填充物。

items.en: English bombast means cotton stuffing for clothes.
items.cn: 英语 bombast 指填塞衣服的棉絮。

items.en: The word moves from stuffing cloth to stuffing words.
items.cn: 这个词由填衣转向填词。

items.en: The adjective appears for inflated, empty style.
items.cn: 形容词出现，指浮夸空洞的文风。

items.en: Bombastic is now applied to speeches and prose.
items.cn: 现代 bombastic 多用于演讲与文章。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bomb- stem; the near-meaning group ranks inflated style from pompous to merely swollen.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bomb- 词干；近义组把浮夸风格从自命不凡排到单纯臃肿。

entries.definition: Inflated and empty speech.
entries.definitionCN: 浮夸空洞的言辞。

entries.definition: To attack continuously, with shells or words.
entries.definitionCN: 以炮弹或言语连续攻击。

entries.definition: An explosive device.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸装置。

entries.definition: A shocking piece of news.
entries.definitionCN: 令人震惊的消息。

entries.definition: Showing an inflated sense of importance.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出膨胀的自我重要感。

entries.definition: Using pompous and elaborate language.
entries.definitionCN: 使用夸张华丽的语言。

entries.definition: Swollen in style, dull to read.
entries.definitionCN: 文风臃肿乏味。

entries.definition: Filled with air or exaggerated in style.
entries.definitionCN: 充满空气或风格夸张的。

normalIntro.en: Bombast was the cotton that padded a coat; bombastic speech is padded with wind.
normalIntro.cn: bombast 是填大衣的棉絮；bombastic 的话是用空气填起来的。

normal.en: Bombast first meant cotton padding.
normal.cn: bombast 最初指填塞用棉絮。

normal.en: Padding hides shape; padded words hide meaning.
normal.cn: 填充物遮住形体；注水的词遮住意思。

normal.en: Add -ic and the noun becomes the style.
normal.cn: 加 -ic，名词变成风格形容词。

normal.en: A bombastic speech gets louder and emptier.
normal.cn: 浮夸的演讲越来越响，也越来越空。

normal.en: If you cannot restate the sentence plainly, it may be bombastic.
normal.cn: 若说不出一句朴素的重述，它可能就很浮夸。

abstract.en: A coat worn with nothing inside it.
abstract.cn: 里面什么都没有的大衣。

abstract.en: Volume standing in for meaning.
abstract.cn: 用音量顶替意思。

abstract.en: Words stuffed like a cushion.
abstract.cn: 像靠垫一样被塞满的词语。

examples.en: His bombastic introduction mentioned no actual proposal.
examples.cn: 他浮夸的开场白里没有提出任何实际方案。

examples.en: Critics called the manifesto bombastic and vague.
examples.cn: 批评者称这份宣言浮夸而含糊。

examples.en: The letter is bombastic, but the figures inside are precise.
examples.cn: 这封信写得浮夸，里面的数字却很精确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「表述必夸张」——一开口就要把话说得又大又满，正是浮夸。

root: bombast（填衣棉絮，16 世纪转指「注水的言辞」）+ -ic（形容词后缀）

sensesIntro.en: A stuffed coat and a stuffed sentence are the same object: plenty of material, no shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 塞满的大衣与塞满的句子是同一件东西：材料很多，形制全无。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice rising through grand words that never land
core.cn: 核心意象：声音在宏大的词里升上去，却始终没有落点

branches.en: A simple question given a long loud answer.
branches.cn: 简单问题得到又长又响的回答。

branches.en: Applause after a sentence with no content.
branches.cn: 一句空话之后的掌声。

branches.en: An essay ornamented at every clause.
branches.cn: 每个分句都加了装饰的文章。

branches.en: A report that says little at length.
branches.cn: 说得很长、内容很少的报告。

branches.en: Padding standing where substance should be.
branches.cn: 该有实质之处塞满了填絮。

intro.en: Bombastic is a noun stem plus -ic; the list below builds the style words and the cotton root behind it.
intro.cn: bombastic 是名词词干加 -ic；下面列出风格词汇与背后的「棉」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin bombax is cotton, tumere is to swell, and grandis is grand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bombax 意为棉花，tumere 意为膨胀，grandis 意为宏大。

latinEntries.exampleCN: tumere 产生 tumid 与 tumour。
grandis 产生 grand 与 grandeur。

definition_zh: 令人敬畏的；难对付的；强大的
definition_en: worthy of fear and respect, especially because of strength, skill or reputation
core_image: 一位老将走进会场，争论声立刻低下去，所有人不自觉坐直
scene: 老将一走进会场，争论声立刻低了下去，所有人都坐直了身子。 The redoubtable old general silenced the room simply by entering it.
sceneCN: 这里 redoubtable 指令人敬畏的（第 1 个义项：因力量或声望而让人心生敬畏）；句意为那位令人敬畏的老将一进门就让整个会场安静下来。

pos.zh: 令人敬畏的；难对付的；强大的

senses.title: A redoubtable opponent
senses.definition: of a person, commanding fear and respect by strength or skill
senses.definitionCN: 指人因力量或本领而让人既怕又敬
senses.example: The redoubtable old general silenced the room simply by entering it.
senses.exampleCN: 那位令人敬畏的老将一进门就让整个会场安静下来。
senses.why: The first sense is about a person in the room, felt at once.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项讲的是在场的一个人，感受是即时的。

senses.title: A redoubtable reputation
senses.definition: of a name or a record, strong enough to warn people in advance
senses.definitionCN: 指名声或战绩强到足以事先让人退让
senses.example: The firm had a redoubtable reputation for winning difficult cases.
senses.exampleCN: 这家事务所以能赢下难案而声名令人忌惮。
senses.why: Here the fear arrives before the person does.
senses.whyCN: 这里的畏惧在人来之前就已经到了。

intro.en: Redoubtable comes from Old French redoutable, from redouter, 'to fear greatly', built on douter, 'to doubt'.
intro.cn: redoubtable 来自古法语 redoutable，源头是 redouter（非常惧怕），构词基于 douter（怀疑）。

items.en: Dubitare meant to doubt or hesitate.
items.cn: dubitare 意为怀疑、迟疑。

items.en: Douter carried the sense of fearing as well as doubting.
items.cn: douter 同时有怀疑与惧怕之意。

items.en: Redouter meant to fear someone greatly.
items.cn: redouter 意为非常惧怕某人。

items.en: The adjective meant to be feared.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「值得惧怕的」。

items.en: English softened fear into awe and respect.
items.cn: 英语把恐惧柔化成了敬畏与尊重。

note.en: The look-alike group is the doubt- family, which shares the root of hesitation; the near-meaning group separates formidable, daunting, awe-inspiring and fearsome.
note.cn: 形近组是 doubt 词族，共享「迟疑」的词根；近义组把「难对付的」「吓人的」「令人叹服的」「可怕的」分开。

entries.definition: a small defensive fort.
entries.definitionCN: 一座小型防御堡垒。

entries.definition: feared and respected, in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 旧用法中令人敬畏的。

entries.definition: uncertain or unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定的；不太可能的。

entries.definition: almost certainly.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎肯定地。

entries.definition: hard to deal with because of size or skill.
entries.definitionCN: 因规模或本领而难对付的。

entries.definition: discouraging by its difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 因困难而令人却步的。

entries.definition: filling a person with wonder and fear.
entries.definitionCN: 使人充满惊叹与敬畏的。

entries.definition: causing fear by appearance or strength.
entries.definitionCN: 因外表或力量引起恐惧的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a room going quiet as an old general steps through the door.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「老将一跨进门，整个房间就安静下来」的画面。

normal.en: Redoubtable hides the word doubt: people are afraid to doubt him.
normal.cn: redoubtable 里藏着 doubt：没人敢怀疑他。

normal.en: Picture every back straightening as he walks in.
normal.cn: 想象他走进来时每一根脊背都挺直了。

normal.en: Say rih-DOW-tuh-bl; DOW carries the stress.
normal.cn: 读 rih-DOW-tuh-bl，重音在 DOW。

normal.en: It is fear in the first half, respect in the second.
normal.cn: 前半是恐惧，后半是尊重。

normal.en: Ask whether the fear comes from what he did or from what he might do.
normal.cn: 问这份畏惧来自他做过的事，还是他可能做的事。

abstract.en: Redoubtable is the compliment that still smells of threat.
abstract.cn: 令人敬畏是一个仍带着威胁气味的赞美。

abstract.en: A reputation becomes redoubtable when nobody wants to test it.
abstract.cn: 当没人愿意去试的时候，名声就变得令人忌惮。

abstract.en: The word grew out of doubt and settled into awe.
abstract.cn: 这个词从怀疑里长大，最后住进了敬畏。

examples.en: The redoubtable old general silenced the room simply by entering it.
examples.cn: 那位令人敬畏的老将一进门就让整个会场安静下来。

examples.en: The firm had a redoubtable reputation for winning difficult cases.
examples.cn: 这家事务所以能赢下难案而声名令人忌惮。

examples.en: She was redoubtable in debate, and no one interrupted her.
examples.cn: 她在辩论中令人忌惮，没有人敢打断她。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（加强）+ doubt（怀疑、惧怕）+ able → 让人不敢怀疑、也不敢轻视的。

root: 古法语 redoutable → redouter（惧怕）→ re- + douter（怀疑，拉丁语 dubitare）

sensesIntro.en: Two senses carry one threat: a person feared in the room, and a name feared before the person arrives.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项带着同一种威胁：在场就让人畏惧的人，以及人还没到名声先到的姓名。

core.en: A ROOM GOING QUIET
core.cn: 安静下来的房间

branches.en: A present person who commands fear and respect.
branches.cn: 在场就令人又怕又敬的人。

branches.en: A reputation that warns before the person comes.
branches.cn: 在人来之前先发出警告的名声。

branches.en: One is felt in the body, the other heard in advance.
branches.cn: 一个在身体上感到，一个事先听到。

branches.en: Old generals and strong debaters fill the first sense.
branches.cn: 老将与强辩者填满第一个义项。

branches.en: Firms and families fill the second.
branches.cn: 事务所与家族填满第二个。

intro.en: The doubt- family is about hesitation: doubt, doubtful, doubtless and redoubtable all descend from dubitare.
intro.cn: doubt 词族讲的是迟疑：doubt、doubtful、doubtless、redoubtable 都出自 dubitare。

latinIntro.en: Latin dubitare, 'to doubt', became French douter, 'to fear'; the re- in redouter makes the fear very great.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dubitare（怀疑）变成法语 douter（惧怕）；redouter 里的 re- 把这份惧怕加大。

definition_zh: 文化传递；文化通过社会学习在人与人、代与代之间传递的过程
definition_en: the passing on of culture through social learning between people and across generations
core_image: 一双布满老茧的手把工具递给一双年轻的手，动作、节奏与禁忌都随工具一起交出去
scene: 老人把手艺一遍遍示范给孙辈，歌谣与禁忌也随同一双手传下去。 Weaving skills pass from grandmother to granddaughter by cultural transmission rather than by written rules.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural transmission 指「文化经社会学习在代际之间传递」（第 1 个义项：文化传递的总过程）；句意为织布技艺靠文化传递从祖母传到孙女，而非靠成文规则。可辨识物件：织机、双手、线轴、歌谣、家屋。

pos.zh: 文化传递（人类学术语，常作不可数）
一次具体的文化传递（可数）

senses.title: Social learning across generations
senses.definition: the passing of customs, skills and beliefs through teaching and imitation rather than genes
senses.definitionCN: 风俗、技能与信念经教导与模仿而非基因传递
senses.example: Weaving skills pass from grandmother to granddaughter by cultural transmission rather than by written rules.
senses.exampleCN: 织布技艺靠文化传递从祖母传到孙女，而非靠成文规则。
senses.why: Culture is what people learn from other people; transmission names the channel that carries it beyond one lifetime.
senses.whyCN: 文化是人向他人学来的东西；传递指把它带出单个人一生的通道。

senses.title: Vertical transmission
senses.definition: the passing of culture from parents to children
senses.definitionCN: 文化由父母传给孩子
senses.example: Vertical cultural transmission explains why dialects follow family lines.
senses.exampleCN: 纵向文化传递解释了为何方言沿着家族线分布。
senses.why: The family is the first channel, and the parent-to-child direction is the one most easily observed.
senses.whyCN: 家庭是第一通道，父母到孩子的方向也是最容易观察到的。

senses.title: Horizontal transmission
senses.definition: the passing of culture between peers of the same generation
senses.definitionCN: 同代同伴之间的文化传递
senses.example: Fashions spread by horizontal cultural transmission among classmates.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚通过同学之间的横向文化传递扩散。
senses.why: Peers teach each other sideways, which is why a schoolyard can change faster than a household.
senses.whyCN: 同伴横向互教，因此校园的品味变化可能比家庭更快。

senses.title: Oblique transmission
senses.definition: the passing of culture from non-parental adults of the older generation
senses.definitionCN: 由非父母的上一代成年人传递文化
senses.example: Oblique cultural transmission happens through aunts, teachers and neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 斜向文化传递通过姑姨、教师与邻居发生。
senses.why: Adults other than parents also transmit, and anthropology gives this diagonal route its own name.
senses.whyCN: 父母以外的成年人也在传递，人类学给这条斜线路径单独命名。

senses.title: Language and oral tradition
senses.definition: the passing of language, songs and stories by speech
senses.definitionCN: 语言、歌谣与故事经口头传递
senses.example: Oral poetry survives by cultural transmission long after its first singers are forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 口头诗歌靠文化传递留存，远在其最早的歌者被遗忘之后。
senses.why: Speech is the lightest carrier: it needs no object, only a listener who repeats.
senses.whyCN: 言语是最轻的载体：它不需要物件，只需要一个会复述的听者。

senses.title: Skills and apprenticeship
senses.definition: the passing of practical skills through demonstration and practice
senses.definitionCN: 实用技能经示范与练习传递
senses.example: The workshop keeps cultural transmission alive by pairing masters with beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工坊通过师徒配对让文化传递延续。
senses.why: Skills that live in the hands must be shown, not merely described, so apprenticeship is a distinct channel.
